title: 〜を〜に任せる
meaning: to leave (a matter) up to; to entrust (something) to (someone)
summary: 任せる assigns responsibility for something to another person or faculty: the thing entrusted is marked with を and the person or thing you leave it to with に. 仕事を彼に任せる = leave the work to him, 判断を現場に任せる = leave the decision to the people on site. It can also mean giving oneself over to something (運を天に任せる, 想像に任せる). The sense is that you hand over control and let the other side decide or act.
pitfalls: Mark the entrusted thing with を and the person you leave it to with に: 仕事を部下に任せる.
任せる also appears as 〜に任せて meaning 'giving free rein to (force or emotion)', as in 力任せ; the core pattern here simply hands over responsibility.

examples.ja: 細かいことは、現場の判断に任せることにした。
examples.en: We decided to leave the fine details up to the judgment of the people on site.
examples.f: ｜細[こま]かいことは、｜現場[げんば]の｜判断[はんだん]に｜任[まか]せることにした。

examples.ja: この件は、経験のある彼に任せたほうがいいだろう。
examples.en: It would probably be better to entrust this matter to him, since he has the experience.
examples.f: この｜件[けん]は、｜経験[けいけん]のある｜彼[かれ]に｜任[まか]せたほうがいいだろう。

title: あげく
meaning: in the end; after all (following a long, often troublesome process)
summary: 〜あげく marks that after much time, effort, or trouble, a result finally comes — and that result is usually undesirable or regrettable. さんざん迷ったあげく = after hesitating a great deal, in the end. It follows a た-form verb or a noun + の, and often appears as あげくに or あげくの果てに. Use it to stress that a drawn-out process led to a (frequently bad) outcome.
pitfalls: The following result is usually negative or regrettable, not a neutral or happy one.
Attach it to the た-form: 迷ったあげく, not 迷うあげく.

examples.ja: 長時間言い争ったあげく、結局結論は出なかった。
examples.en: After arguing for a long time, in the end no conclusion was reached.
examples.f: ｜長時間[ちょうじかん]｜言い争[いいあらそ]ったあげく、｜結局[けっきょく]｜結論[けつろん]は｜出[で]なかった。

examples.ja: さんざん悩んだあげくの決断だったが、後悔はしていない。
examples.en: It was a decision made after agonizing endlessly, but I have no regrets.
examples.f: さんざん｜悩[なや]んだあげくの｜決断[けつだん]だったが、｜後悔[こうかい]はしていない。

synonyms.note: た末に also marks 'after much ~, finally', but is more neutral and can lead to a positive result; あげく leans negative.

related.note: 結果 states a neutral 'as a result of ~'; あげく adds that the process was long and trying and the outcome regrettable.

title: 後(の)
meaning: ... more; ... left; the remaining
summary: As an adverb, あと + a quantity means '~ more / ~ to go' toward a total — あと少し = a little more, あと五分 = five more minutes. As 後の + a noun it means 'the remaining ~ / the rest of the ~' (後の半分 = the other half). In both uses it counts what is still left over. It is common in everyday speech when tallying what remains.
pitfalls: This あと ('~ more / remaining') counts what is left toward a total; it is not the time word あとで ('later / afterward').

examples.ja: ゴールまで、あと三キロだ。もう少し頑張ろう。
examples.en: It's three more kilometers to the goal. Let's push on a little longer.
examples.f: ゴールまで、あと｜三[さん]キロだ。もう｜少[すこ]し｜頑張[がんば]ろう。

examples.ja: 席はあと二つしか残っていないので、早めに予約したほうがいい。
examples.en: There are only two seats left, so it's better to book early.
examples.f: ｜席[せき]はあと｜二[ふた]つしか｜残[のこ]っていないので、｜早[はや]めに｜予約[よやく]したほうがいい。

title: いきなり
meaning: suddenly; abruptly; without warning
summary: いきなり describes an action that happens abruptly with no lead-up, preparation, or warning — often skipping the steps you would normally expect. いきなり本題に入る = jump straight into the main topic, いきなり泣き出す = burst into tears out of nowhere. The emphasis is on the absence of any preliminary stage, which often makes the action surprising.
pitfalls: いきなり stresses that there was no warning or preparation, not merely that something happened 'quickly'.
Compared with 急に (a sudden change of state), いきなり highlights the lack of any expected lead-up or first step.

examples.ja: 彼は挨拶もせず、いきなり本題を切り出した。
examples.en: Without even a greeting, he abruptly launched into the main point.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜挨拶[あいさつ]もせず、いきなり｜本題[ほんだい]を｜切り出[きりだ]した。

examples.ja: 前を歩いていた人が、いきなり立ち止まった。
examples.en: The person walking ahead of me suddenly stopped without warning.
examples.f: ｜前[まえ]を｜歩[ある]いていた｜人[ひと]が、いきなり｜立ち止[たちど]まった。

title: 以上に
meaning: more than; beyond; even more than
summary: 〜以上に marks that something exceeds a stated standard — 'more than ~, beyond ~'. 思った以上に = more than I thought, 予想以上に = beyond expectations, 必要以上に = more than necessary. It attaches to a noun or a plain-form verb and signals that the degree surpassed the reference point, often more than anticipated.
pitfalls: 以上に compares degree ('more than'); don't confuse it with 以上は ('now that / since'), which gives a reason.
It often implies surpassing an already high or expected level, not just a plain comparison.

examples.ja: 今年の夏は、去年以上に暑く感じる。
examples.en: This summer feels even hotter than last year.
examples.f: ｜今年[ことし]の｜夏[なつ]は、｜去年[きょねん]｜以上[いじょう]に｜暑[あつ]く｜感[かん]じる。

examples.ja: 会議は、予想以上に長引いてしまった。
examples.en: The meeting dragged on far longer than expected.
examples.f: ｜会議[かいぎ]は、｜予想[よそう]｜以上[いじょう]に｜長引[ながび]いてしまった。

synonyms.note: より marks a straightforward comparison ('than'); 以上に stresses exceeding an already high or expected level.

title: 以上は
meaning: now that; since; given that
summary: 〜以上は presents an established fact as firm grounds, so that a fitting resolve, duty, or natural conclusion follows — 'now that ~, since ~'. 引き受けた以上は = now that I've taken it on, 約束した以上は = since I promised. The second clause typically expresses determination, obligation, or an inevitable consequence rather than a neutral remark.
pitfalls: 以上は gives a reason ('since / now that'); don't confuse it with 以上に ('more than').
The following clause carries resolve, obligation, or a natural conclusion — not a plain neutral statement.

examples.ja: 一度引き受けた以上は、最後まで責任を持ってやります。
examples.en: Now that I've taken it on, I'll see it through to the end with full responsibility.
examples.f: ｜一度[いちど]｜引き受[ひきう]けた｜以上[いじょう]は、｜最後[さいご]まで｜責任[せきにん]を｜持[も]ってやります。

examples.ja: 社会人である以上は、時間を守るのは当然のことだ。
examples.en: Since one is a working adult, keeping to schedule is only natural.
examples.f: ｜社会[しゃかい]｜人[じん]である｜以上[いじょう]は、｜時間[じかん]を｜守[まも]るのは｜当然[とうぜん]のことだ。

synonyms.note: からには is very close in meaning and more common in speech; 以上は is somewhat more formal.
上は also means 'now that', but is more literary and follows a verb of decision or action already taken.

title: 一応
meaning: tentatively; more or less; just in case; for now
summary: 一応 marks that something is done only to a minimal or provisional degree — enough for now, not thoroughly. It has two shades: 'tentatively / more or less' (一応終わった = it's more or less done) and 'just in case / for form's sake' (一応確認しておく = check it just to be safe). Either way it signals a basic, non-exhaustive level rather than a complete or definitive one.
pitfalls: 一応 downplays thoroughness — 'more or less / just for now', not 'completely'; it often hedges that a task is only provisionally done.

examples.ja: 一応目を通しましたが、細かいところはまだ確認していません。
examples.en: I've looked it over more or less, but I haven't checked the finer points yet.
examples.f: ｜一応[いちおう]｜目[め]を｜通[とお]しましたが、｜細[こま]かいところはまだ｜確認[かくにん]していません。

examples.ja: 使わないかもしれないが、一応傘を持っていこう。
examples.en: I might not use it, but I'll take an umbrella just in case.
examples.f: ｜使[つか]わないかもしれないが、｜一応[いちおう]｜傘[かさ]を｜持[も]っていこう。

related.note: 一旦 means 'once (one does)' or 'temporarily'; 一応 means 'tentatively / just in case', stressing a minimal degree.

title: 一気に
meaning: in one go; all at once; in one breath
summary: 一気に says an action is carried out in a single continuous burst, without pausing along the way — 一気に飲む = drink in one gulp, 一気に読む = read straight through. It stresses momentum and the absence of any interruption, often conveying vigor or a sudden surge. Use it when something is done from start to finish in one unbroken stretch.
pitfalls: 一気に stresses one unbroken, continuous burst; 一度に stresses several things happening at the same time.

examples.ja: 面白くて、その小説を一気に読んでしまった。
examples.en: It was so gripping that I read the novel straight through in one sitting.
examples.f: ｜面白[おもしろ]くて、その｜小説[しょうせつ]を｜一気[いっき]に｜読[よ]んでしまった。

examples.ja: 残っていた仕事を、午前中に一気に片付けた。
examples.en: I cleared away all the remaining work in one go over the morning.
examples.f: ｜残[のこ]っていた｜仕事[しごと]を、｜午前[ごぜん]｜中[ちゅう]に｜一気[いっき]に｜片付[かたづ]けた。

synonyms.note: 一度に stresses simultaneity ('all at the same time'); 一気に stresses momentum with no pause.

title: 一旦
meaning: once (one does); for the moment; temporarily
summary: 一旦 has two related uses. First, 'once ~ (has happened), then ...', setting up a condition after which a state holds — 一旦決めたら = once you've decided (it's hard to reverse). Second, 'for the moment / temporarily', marking a provisional pause — 一旦中止する = suspend for now. It is fairly formal and common in writing and announcements.
pitfalls: In the 'once ~' sense it sets up a condition, so it typically pairs with たら or ば.
In the 'for now' sense it implies a temporary halt that may resume, not a permanent stop.

examples.ja: 一旦決めたことは、簡単には変えないほうがいい。
examples.en: Once you've decided something, it's better not to change it lightly.
examples.f: ｜一旦[いったん]｜決[き]めたことは、｜簡単[かんたん]には｜変[か]えないほうがいい。

examples.ja: 工事は、天候の悪化で一旦中止となった。
examples.en: The construction was halted for the time being due to worsening weather.
examples.f: ｜工事[こうじ]は、｜天候[てんこう]の｜悪化[あっか]で｜一旦[いったん]｜中止[ちゅうし]となった。

related.note: 一応 means 'tentatively / just in case'; 一旦 means 'once (one does)' or 'temporarily'.

title: いつの間にか
meaning: before one knows it; without noticing; at some unnoticed point
summary: いつの間にか says a change took place at some point you never noticed — you only realize it after the fact. いつの間にか眠っていた = I had fallen asleep before I knew it. It emphasizes that the moment of change slipped by unobserved, and it pairs naturally with a resulting state such as 〜ていた. Use it for changes that quietly happened while your attention was elsewhere.
pitfalls: It describes noticing a change only afterward; the point is that the change went unobserved, so it often ends in 〜ていた.

examples.ja: 話に夢中になっていて、いつの間にか終電を逃していた。
examples.en: I was so absorbed in the conversation that I missed the last train without realizing it.
examples.f: ｜話[はなし]に｜夢中[むちゅう]になっていて、いつの｜間[ま]にか｜終電[しゅうでん]を｜逃[のが]していた。

examples.ja: 子どもは、いつの間にかこんなに大きくなっていた。
examples.en: The children had grown this big before I even noticed.
examples.f: ｜子[こ]どもは、いつの｜間[ま]にかこんなに｜大[おお]きくなっていた。

related.note: うちに frames doing something within a period ('while / before'); いつの間にか marks a change you failed to notice.

title: 未だに
meaning: still; even now; to this day
summary: 未だに stresses that a state has persisted unchanged right up to the present, usually with a note of surprise or dissatisfaction that it has not changed — 未だに返事がない = still no reply even now. It carries the nuance that the situation really ought to have changed by this point. It is stronger and more formal than a plain まだ, and often appears with a negative or 〜ている.
pitfalls: 未だに carries lingering surprise or discontent that a state persists 'even now'; it is stronger and more formal than plain まだ.
It typically goes with a negative or a 〜ている state, not a one-time action.

examples.ja: あの事故の原因は、未だにはっきりしていない。
examples.en: The cause of that accident is still not clear to this day.
examples.f: あの｜事故[じこ]の｜原因[げんいん]は、｜未[いま]だにはっきりしていない。

examples.ja: 卒業して十年たつが、未だに彼とは連絡を取り合っている。
examples.en: Ten years have passed since graduation, yet even now he and I keep in touch.
examples.f: ｜卒業[そつぎょう]して｜十[じゅう]｜年[ねん]たつが、｜未[いま]だに｜彼[かれ]とは｜連絡[れんらく]を｜取り合[とりあ]っている。

title: いよいよ
meaning: at last; finally; the moment approaches; increasingly
summary: いよいよ marks that a long-awaited moment is finally at hand, building a sense of anticipation as it draws near — いよいよ明日が本番だ = at last, tomorrow is the real thing. It can also mean 'more and more / increasingly' when a tendency intensifies (いよいよ激しくなる = grow ever more intense). The core feeling is mounting tension toward a climax.
pitfalls: いよいよ builds anticipation that an awaited moment has arrived; ついに reports that something finally happened as an outcome.
It has a second sense, 'more and more', when a trend steadily intensifies.

examples.ja: 長い準備期間を経て、いよいよ開店の日を迎えた。
examples.en: After a long preparation period, opening day has at last arrived.
examples.f: ｜長[なが]い｜準備[じゅんび]｜期間[きかん]を｜経[へ]て、いよいよ｜開店[かいてん]の｜日[ひ]を｜迎[むか]えた。

examples.ja: 台風が近づき、風がいよいよ強くなってきた。
examples.en: As the typhoon drew near, the wind grew ever stronger.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]が｜近[ちか]づき、｜風[かぜ]がいよいよ｜強[つよ]くなってきた。

synonyms.note: ついに reports that something finally came about as a result; いよいよ conveys the mounting anticipation as the moment approaches.

title: いわゆる
meaning: so-called; what is known as; what people call
summary: いわゆる comes before a noun to flag it as 'the so-called ~ / what is known as ~', pointing to a common label or well-known term. いわゆる勝ち組 = the so-called winners. It introduces a widely used designation, and can carry a slight distance, as if noting that this is merely what people call it. It modifies a noun directly, like a prenominal adjective.
pitfalls: いわゆる attaches directly to a noun (いわゆる常識), not to a verb or a whole sentence.
It labels something with a common term, sometimes hinting the label is not the speaker's own choice of words.

examples.ja: 彼は、いわゆるエリートコースを歩んできた人だ。
examples.en: He's someone who has walked what you'd call the elite path.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は、いわゆるエリートコースを｜歩[あゆ]んできた｜人[ひと]だ。

examples.ja: これが、いわゆる「五月病」というものです。
examples.en: This is what is known as 'May sickness.'
examples.f: これが、いわゆる「｜五月[ごがつ]｜病[びょう]」というものです。

title: 上は
meaning: now that; since (one has done)
summary: 〜上は presents a decisive fact — usually a decision made or an action already taken — as grounds for the resolve or obligation that follows. 引き受けた上は = now that I've undertaken it. The second clause states determination or what must naturally be done. It is formal and somewhat literary; in everyday speech からには is more usual.
pitfalls: 上は is formal and follows a verb of decision or action already taken; the second clause expresses resolve or obligation.
In conversation, からには is the more natural choice.

examples.ja: 会社を辞めると決めた上は、迷わず前に進むだけだ。
examples.en: Now that I've decided to leave the company, all that's left is to move forward without hesitation.
examples.f: ｜会社[かいしゃ]を｜辞[や]めると｜決[き]めた｜上[うえ]は、｜迷[まよ]わず｜前[まえ]に｜進[すす]むだけだ。

examples.ja: 試合に出る上は、優勝を目指して全力を尽くすつもりだ。
examples.en: Since I'm taking part in the match, I intend to aim for victory and give it my all.
examples.f: ｜試合[しあい]に｜出[で]る｜上[うえ]は、｜優勝[ゆうしょう]を｜目指[めざ]して｜全力[ぜんりょく]を｜尽[つ]くすつもりだ。

synonyms.note: 以上は is very close in meaning; 上は is more literary and centers on a decision or action already taken.
からには is the everyday, conversational equivalent; 上は is more formal and written.

title: 〜得ない
meaning: cannot; there is no possibility of; it is unthinkable that
summary: 〜得ない (read えない) attaches to the ます-stem to say that something is impossible or unthinkable — あり得ない = cannot be / impossible, 考え得ない = inconceivable. It is the negative counterpart of 〜得る and belongs to formal, often written, register. It denies that a thing could possibly happen, rather than saying someone lacks the skill to do it.
pitfalls: In the negative, 得 is always read え: あり得ない (ありえない), never ありうない.
It denies possibility ('this cannot happen'), not personal ability ('I can't do it well').

examples.ja: そんな単純なミスを彼がするとは、考え得ない。
examples.en: It's inconceivable that he would make such a simple mistake.
examples.f: そんな｜単純[たんじゅん]なミスを｜彼[かれ]がするとは、｜考[かんが]え｜得[え]ない。

examples.ja: 想定し得ない事態が、次々と起こった。
examples.en: Situations that could not have been anticipated occurred one after another.
examples.f: ｜想定[そうてい]し｜得[え]ない｜事態[じたい]が、｜次々[つぎつぎ]と｜起[お]こった。

antonyms.note: 〜得る is the affirmative 'can happen / is possible'; 〜得ない denies that possibility.

related.note: かねる expresses difficulty or reluctance ('cannot bring oneself to'); 得ない denies that a thing is possible at all.

title: 〜得る
meaning: can; be possible; could (happen)
summary: 〜得る (read either える or うる) attaches to the ます-stem to say that something is possible or could occur — あり得る = can happen / is possible, 起こり得る = could occur. It is formal and common in writing and discussion. It expresses that a situation is within the realm of possibility, which is distinct from the potential form meaning personal 'can do'.
pitfalls: The dictionary form is read both える and うる (あり得る = ありうる or ありえる), but the negative is only えない.
It states possibility ('could happen'), which differs from the potential 'can (do something)'.

examples.ja: これは誰にでも起こり得る問題だから、油断できない。
examples.en: This is a problem that could happen to anyone, so we can't let our guard down.
examples.f: これは｜誰[だれ]にでも｜起[お]こり｜得[え]る｜問題[もんだい]だから、｜油断[ゆだん]できない。

examples.ja: その計画は、理論上は十分にあり得る。
examples.en: That plan is entirely possible, at least in theory.
examples.f: その｜計画[けいかく]は、｜理論[りろん]｜上[じょう]は｜十分[じゅうぶん]にあり｜得[え]る。

antonyms.note: 〜得ない is the negative 'cannot happen / is impossible'; 〜得る affirms the possibility.

related.note: かねない carries a negative likelihood ('might well (do something bad)'); 〜得る is a neutral statement that something is possible.

title: お〜願う
meaning: to (humbly) request that you ~; we ask you to ~
summary: お＋a verb stem＋願う (or ご＋a Sino-Japanese noun＋願う) forms a very polite, businesslike request that the listener do something — お待ち願います = I ask that you wait, ご了承願います = I ask for your understanding. It is common in announcements, notices, and formal correspondence. The request is directed at the listener's action and is normally used in the 願います / 願いたい form.
pitfalls: Keep it polite (願います / 願いたく), as bare 願う can sound blunt.
Use ご with Sino-Japanese nouns (ご確認願います) and お with native verb stems (お待ち願います).

examples.ja: ご不明な点がございましたら、お問い合わせ願います。
examples.en: Should there be any points that are unclear, please make an inquiry.
examples.f: ご｜不明[ふめい]な｜点[てん]がございましたら、お｜問い合[といあ]わせ｜願[ねが]います。

examples.ja: 危険ですので、白線の内側までお下がり願います。
examples.en: As it is dangerous, we ask you to step back behind the white line.
examples.f: ｜危険[きけん]ですので、｜白線[はくせん]の｜内側[うちがわ]までお｜下[さ]がり｜願[ねが]います。

related.note: お〜する humbles the speaker's OWN action; お〜願う asks the LISTENER to perform an action.
てください is a plainer polite request; お〜願う is more formal and typical of notices and business settings.

title: おおよそ
meaning: roughly; approximately; in general
summary: おおよそ is an adverb meaning 'roughly / approximately', giving an inexact figure or a broad outline — おおよそ二時間かかる = takes roughly two hours, おおよその見当がつく = get a rough idea. It can also mean 'generally / by and large'. It is slightly formal; およそ is the shorter, more common variant. It stands before the amount or statement it qualifies.
pitfalls: おおよそ is an adverb placed before the amount (おおよそ十人); the suffix くらい follows the amount (十人くらい).
It gives an approximate whole and can also mean 'by and large / on the whole'.

examples.ja: 工事の完了まで、おおよそ半年かかる見込みです。
examples.en: It is expected to take roughly half a year until the construction is complete.
examples.f: ｜工事[こうじ]の｜完了[かんりょう]まで、おおよそ｜半年[はんとし]かかる｜見込[みこ]みです。

examples.ja: 話を聞いて、事情はおおよそ理解できた。
examples.en: Having heard the account, I understood the circumstances more or less.
examples.f: ｜話[はなし]を｜聞[き]いて、｜事情[じじょう]はおおよそ｜理解[りかい]できた。

synonyms.note: くらい marks approximation as a suffix after a number (十人くらい); おおよそ is an adverb standing before it.

title: 恐らく
meaning: probably; most likely; in all likelihood
summary: 恐らく marks the speaker's fairly confident conjecture — 'probably / most likely'. It usually pairs with a following だろう, でしょう, or に違いない. 恐らく間に合わないだろう = we probably won't make it in time. It is more formal than たぶん and often leans toward a serious or unfavorable guess. Despite the kanji 恐, it has nothing to do with fear.
structure: 恐らく＋Sentence（〜だろう／でしょう）
pitfalls: 恐らく normally co-occurs with だろう / でしょう / に違いない at the end of the sentence.
The kanji 恐 does not carry a sense of 'fear' here; the word simply means 'probably'.

examples.ja: このままだと、恐らく今日じゅうには終わらないだろう。
examples.en: At this rate, we probably won't finish within today.
examples.f: このままだと、｜恐[おそ]らく｜今日[きょう]じゅうには｜終[お]わらないだろう。

examples.ja: 空の様子から見て、恐らく午後から天気が崩れるでしょう。
examples.en: Judging by the look of the sky, the weather will most likely turn in the afternoon.
examples.f: ｜空[そら]の｜様子[ようす]から｜見[み]て、｜恐[おそ]らく｜午後[ごご]から｜天気[てんき]が｜崩[くず]れるでしょう。

related.note: に違いない expresses near-certainty; 恐らく is a weaker, more tentative 'probably'.

title: 恐れがある
meaning: there is a risk/danger that (something undesirable may happen)
summary: 恐れがある follows a verb (dictionary form) or a noun + の and warns that there is a real risk of an undesirable outcome. It is formal and largely written — common in news reports, warnings, and forecasts. 恐れ literally means 'fear', so it points to something one would rather avoid.
structure: Noun ＋ の ＋ 恐れがある
pitfalls: Used only for unwelcome outcomes; you would not say 合格する恐れがある for a hoped-for result.
Formal and written; in everyday speech かもしれない sounds more natural.

examples.ja: 台風の影響で、明日は電車が止まる恐れがあります。
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, there is a risk the trains will stop tomorrow.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]の｜影響[えいきょう]で、｜明日[あした]は｜電車[でんしゃ]が｜止[と]まる｜恐[おそ]れがあります。

examples.ja: 誤った使い方をすると、事故につながる恐れがある。
examples.en: If it is used incorrectly, there is a danger it could lead to an accident.
examples.f: ｜誤[あやま]った｜使い方[つかいかた]をすると、｜事故[じこ]につながる｜恐[おそ]れがある。

synonyms.note: かねない also flags a possible bad outcome but attaches to a verb stem and is less formal; 恐れがある reads as an objective warning.

related.note: かもしれない is a neutral 'might', for good or bad; 恐れがある specifically warns of an undesirable risk.

title: おまけに
meaning: on top of that; what's more; to make matters worse
summary: おまけに is a conjunction that adds a further point piling onto what was just said — usually in the same direction, so a second bad thing on top of a bad one (or a second good thing on top of a good one). It often carries the flavor 'and to make matters worse'. It links whole statements, not nouns.
pitfalls: It adds a circumstance in the same direction, not a contrast; use しかし / でも to turn the point around.
It joins statements, so it stands at the head of the added clause, not between two nouns.

examples.ja: 今日は朝から頭が痛くて、おまけに熱まで出てきた。
examples.en: I've had a headache since this morning, and on top of that I've even started running a fever.
examples.f: ｜今日[きょう]は｜朝[あさ]から｜頭[あたま]が｜痛[いた]くて、おまけに｜熱[ねつ]まで｜出[で]てきた。

examples.ja: あの店は値段が安くて、おまけに料理もおいしい。
examples.en: That restaurant is cheap, and what's more the food is delicious too.
examples.f: あの｜店[みせ]は｜値段[ねだん]が｜安[やす]くて、おまけに｜料理[りょうり]もおいしい。

synonyms.note: その上 also means 'on top of that'; おまけに is more colloquial and often tinged with 'to make things worse'.
しかも is a more formal 'moreover'; おまけに sounds casual and everyday.

related.note: さらに adds and intensifies ('furthermore, even more'); おまけに simply tacks on an extra circumstance.

title: 思うように
meaning: the way one wants/expects (very often used in the negative)
summary: 思うように means 'as one wishes / as one expects things to go'. In practice it appears most often with a negative verb — 思うようにいかない, 思うようにできない — to say that things are not going the way one had hoped, usually with a note of frustration.
pitfalls: It most naturally pairs with a negative verb (思うように進まない = it isn't going as I'd hoped); a plain affirmative is comparatively rare.
思うように describes whether things go as one wishes, so it usually implies effort against an obstacle rather than a neutral statement.

examples.ja: けがのせいで、思うように体が動かない。
examples.en: Because of the injury, my body won't move the way I want it to.
examples.f: けがのせいで、｜思[おも]うように｜体[からだ]が｜動[うご]かない。

examples.ja: 準備はしたが、面接では思うように話せなかった。
examples.en: I had prepared, but at the interview I couldn't speak the way I'd hoped.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]はしたが、｜面接[めんせつ]では｜思[おも]うように｜話[はな]せなかった。

synonyms.note: 通りに (as in 思った通り) also means 'as expected', but is neutral; 思うように leans toward whether things go as one wishes, often in the negative.

title: 及び
meaning: and; as well as (formal listing conjunction between nouns)
summary: 及び is a formal conjunction that joins nouns or noun phrases in the sense of 'and'. It belongs to written, official registers — application forms, laws, notices, business documents — where と or や would sound too casual. It connects items in a list, not clauses.
pitfalls: It joins nouns, not clauses or verbs; to link whole sentences use そして or また.
Formal written register only; in conversation use と instead of 及び.

examples.ja: 申込書には、氏名及び住所を記入してください。
examples.en: On the application form, please write your name and address.
examples.f: ｜申込[もうしこみ]｜書[しょ]には、｜氏名[しめい]｜及[およ]び｜住所[じゅうしょ]を｜記入[きにゅう]してください。

examples.ja: 会議には、部長及び課長が出席する予定です。
examples.en: The manager and the section chief are scheduled to attend the meeting.
examples.f: ｜会議[かいぎ]には、｜部長[ぶちょう]｜及[およ]び｜課長[かちょう]が｜出席[しゅっせき]する｜予定[よてい]です。

related.note: 又は is the same formal register but means 'or' (choose one); 及び joins items together as 'and'.
あるいは offers an alternative ('or; or else'); 及び adds items to the same list.

title: か〜ないかのうちに
romaji: ka ~ nai ka no uchi ni
meaning: no sooner had ~ than; the moment ~; barely had X happened when Y
summary: This pattern repeats one verb — first in the dictionary form, then in the ない form — to say that a second event happens almost the very instant the first does: 'X had barely happened when Y'. The two events are nearly simultaneous, and Y typically follows on immediately.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ か ＋ Verb［ない form］＋ か ＋ のうちに
pitfalls: The two verbs must be the same verb, one affirmative and one negative: 着くか着かないかのうちに.
It describes near-simultaneous events observed by the speaker, so the main clause states something that follows right away, not a plan.

examples.ja: ベルが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した。
examples.en: The bell had barely rung when the students dashed out of the classroom.
examples.f: ベルが｜鳴[な]るか｜鳴[な]らないかのうちに、｜生徒[せいと]たちは｜教室[きょうしつ]を｜飛び出[とびだ]した。

examples.ja: 彼はベッドに入るか入らないかのうちに、眠ってしまった。
examples.en: He was barely in bed when he fell fast asleep.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はベッドに｜入[はい]るか｜入[はい]らないかのうちに、｜眠[ねむ]ってしまった。

synonyms.note: た途端 also marks 'the moment after', but follows a past-tense verb; this pattern stresses that the first action had barely finished.
が早いか is a more literary 'as soon as'; か〜ないかのうちに emphasizes the two events overlapping almost to the instant.

related.note: かと思ったら also links two quick events, but adds surprise that the second is unexpected; this pattern is purely about timing.

title: 甲斐がある
meaning: to be worth the effort; for one's effort to pay off
summary: 甲斐がある says that an effort was worthwhile because it produced a good result. It commonly attaches to a past-tense verb or a noun + の, and often appears in the connective form 甲斐があって ('thanks to the effort, ...'). かい means the worth or reward of what one put in.
structure: Verb［た form］＋ 甲斐がある
Noun ＋ の ＋ 甲斐がある
pitfalls: It is positive — the effort yielded a good outcome; the negative 甲斐がない or 甲斐もなく means the effort was in vain.
It is frequently used connectively as 甲斐があって to lead into the good result.

examples.ja: 毎日練習した甲斐があって、大会で優勝できた。
examples.en: Practicing every day paid off, and I was able to win the tournament.
examples.f: ｜毎日[まいにち]｜練習[れんしゅう]した｜甲斐[かい]があって、｜大会[たいかい]で｜優勝[ゆうしょう]できた。

examples.ja: 苦労して育てた甲斐があり、庭のバラが見事に咲いた。
examples.en: The trouble I took to grow them paid off, and the roses in the garden bloomed beautifully.
examples.f: ｜苦労[くろう]して｜育[そだ]てた｜甲斐[かい]があり、｜庭[にわ]のバラが｜見事[みごと]に｜咲[さ]いた。

synonyms.note: だけのことはある also ties a good result to what was invested ('no wonder, given the effort/status'); 甲斐がある focuses on the effort proving worthwhile.

antonyms.note: 甲斐もなく is the negative counterpart — the effort came to nothing; 甲斐がある says it was rewarded.

title: が気になる
meaning: to be bothered by; to be concerned or curious about (it weighs on your mind)
summary: Noun + が気になる says that something weighs on your mind so that you cannot stop thinking about it — whether from worry or from curiosity. The thing that catches your attention is the subject, marked by が. The feeling is spontaneous: it draws your attention on its own.
structure: Sentence ＋ か ＋ が気になる
pitfalls: 気になる is spontaneous ('it bothers me / catches my attention'); 気にする is the deliberate act of minding or worrying about something.
The thing on your mind is marked with が, not を: 結果が気になる, not 結果を気になる.

examples.ja: 試験の結果が気になって、昨夜はよく眠れなかった。
examples.en: I was so concerned about the exam results that I couldn't sleep well last night.
examples.f: ｜試験[しけん]の｜結果[けっか]が｜気[き]になって、｜昨夜[さくや]はよく｜眠[ねむ]れなかった。

examples.ja: 彼が何を考えているのか気になる。
examples.en: I'm curious about what he is thinking.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]が｜何[なに]を｜考[かんが]えているのか｜気[き]になる。

related.note: This is one member of the wider family of 気 expressions about one's state of mind.
に気がつく is to notice or realize something at a moment; が気になる is a lingering concern that stays on your mind.

title: 限り
meaning: as long as; as far as; within the limits of
summary: 限り sets a boundary on a statement. Its main senses are 'as long as / so long as' a condition holds (Vる・Nである限り), and 'as far as' the speaker's information reaches (見る限り, 知る限り). The core idea is that the main clause is true only within the limit or scope named.
structure: Verb［dictionary form／ない form］＋ 限り
pitfalls: In the 'as long as' sense, the condition bounds the statement: once the condition ends, the claim no longer holds.
知る限り・見る限り mean 'as far as I know/can see', limiting a judgment to the information available, not making an absolute claim.

examples.ja: 私が知る限り、彼はそんなことをする人ではない。
examples.en: As far as I know, he is not the kind of person who would do such a thing.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]が｜知[し]る｜限[かぎ]り、｜彼[かれ]はそんなことをする｜人[ひと]ではない。

examples.ja: 体が健康である限り、働き続けたい。
examples.en: As long as I stay healthy, I want to keep working.
examples.f: ｜体[からだ]が｜健康[けんこう]である｜限[かぎ]り、｜働[はたら]き｜続[つづ]けたい。

related.note: に限る comes from the same root but means 'nothing beats ~ / be limited to ~'; 限り sets the scope of a condition or judgment.
とは限らない, also from 限る, means 'not necessarily'; 限り marks the boundary within which a statement is valid.

title: がけに
meaning: on the way to/from; in the course of going or returning
summary: 〜がけに attaches to the ます-stem of a few motion verbs — chiefly 行き, 帰り, 出かけ — to mean 'on the way there/back', doing something in the course of going or coming home. 帰りがけに is 'on the way home'. It is limited to these set motion stems rather than being freely productive.
pitfalls: It attaches mainly to 行き・帰り・出かけ and similar motion stems; you cannot form it freely from any verb.
This がけ means 'on the way / in the course of going'; it is unrelated to the noun 崖 ('cliff').

examples.ja: 帰りがけに、スーパーで牛乳を買ってきた。
examples.en: On the way home, I picked up some milk at the supermarket.
examples.f: ｜帰[かえ]りがけに、スーパーで｜牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]を｜買[か]ってきた。

examples.ja: 出かけがけに電話が鳴って、少し遅れてしまった。
examples.en: Just as I was heading out, the phone rang, and I ended up a little late.
examples.f: ｜出[で]かけがけに｜電話[でんわ]が｜鳴[な]って、｜少[すこ]し｜遅[おく]れてしまった。

synonyms.note: ついでに means taking the opportunity of one action to also do another; がけに specifically fixes the timing to going or coming back.

related.note: 途中で means 'partway / on the way' more broadly; がけに is tied to the moment of setting out or returning.
がてら (formal) means doing B while doing A, using A's trip for B; がけに just marks 'on the way' of a going/returning verb.

title: かと思ったら・かと思うと
kana: かとおもったら・かとおもうと
romaji: ka to omottara / ka to omou to
meaning: just when; no sooner had ~ than; and then, unexpectedly
summary: [plain form] + かと思ったら / かと思うと links two events in quick succession, where the second is often surprising or the opposite of what the first would lead you to expect: 'just when I thought X, (to my surprise) Y'. The speaker is describing something observed, not planning it.
structure: Verb［plain form］＋ かと思ったら／かと思うと
Sentence ＋ かと思ったら／かと思うと
pitfalls: It reports something the speaker observes; do not use it for your own intended actions.
The second event is typically a sudden or unexpected change right after the first, not a calm continuation.

examples.ja: 空が暗くなったかと思うと、急に雷が鳴り始めた。
examples.en: Just as the sky darkened, thunder suddenly began to rumble.
examples.f: ｜空[そら]が｜暗[くら]くなったかと｜思[おも]うと、｜急[きゅう]に｜雷[かみなり]が｜鳴[な]り｜始[はじ]めた。

examples.ja: さっきまで泣いていたかと思ったら、もう笑っている。
examples.en: One moment ago he was crying, and now he's already laughing.
examples.f: さっきまで｜泣[な]いていたかと｜思[おも]ったら、もう｜笑[わら]っている。

synonyms.note: か〜ないかのうちに also marks 'barely had X happened when Y', but focuses purely on the near-simultaneous timing without the note of surprise.
た途端 means 'the moment after', usually a sudden event; かと思ったら adds that the second thing runs counter to expectation.

related.note: かと思いきや is a more literary cousin stressing that reality contradicted a mistaken assumption; かと思ったら is the everyday form.

title: かねない
meaning: might well (do something bad); could end up ~; is capable of
summary: Verb stem + かねない says that an undesirable outcome is quite possible — 'might well happen / could well end up doing'. It always points to a bad or worrying result. It is the negated form of かねる, and the pair together are a favorite source of confusion.
pitfalls: It is only for undesirable possibilities: 事故を起こしかねない, never a welcome result.
Attach it to the ます-stem: やりかねない, not やるかねない.

examples.ja: そんな無理な計画では、失敗しかねない。
examples.en: With such an unreasonable plan, it could well end in failure.
examples.f: そんな｜無理[むり]な｜計画[けいかく]では、｜失敗[しっぱい]しかねない。

examples.ja: 寝不足が続くと、体を壊しかねません。
examples.en: If you keep going without enough sleep, you could well ruin your health.
examples.f: ｜寝不足[ねぶそく]が｜続[つづ]くと、｜体[からだ]を｜壊[こわ]しかねません。

synonyms.note: 恐れがある also warns of a bad possibility but is more formal and follows a dictionary-form verb or noun; かねない attaches to the stem.
かもしれない is a neutral 'might' for any outcome; かねない specifically implies the possibility is a bad one.

related.note: かねる (affirmative) means 'cannot / find it hard to do'; かねない is its negation but has drifted to mean 'might well (do something bad)'.

title: かねる
meaning: to be unable to; to find it hard to (do) — often a polite refusal
summary: Verb stem + かねる means the speaker cannot, or finds it difficult to, do something. It very often works as a polite refusal — お答えしかねます softens a 'no'. It is not physical impossibility but an inability or reluctance given the circumstances, and it belongs to formal, business-like speech.
pitfalls: Attach it to the ます-stem: 分かりかねる, not 分かるかねる.
It is a formal way to decline, meaning 'I am not able to'; it does not literally mean 'I hate to'.

examples.ja: 申し訳ありませんが、その件についてはお答えしかねます。
examples.en: I'm very sorry, but I am unable to answer regarding that matter.
examples.f: ｜申し訳[もうしわけ]ありませんが、その｜件[けん]についてはお｜答[こた]えしかねます。

examples.ja: お客様のご要望には、こちらでは対応しかねます。
examples.en: We are unable to accommodate your request here.
examples.f: お｜客様[きゃくさま]のご｜要望[ようぼう]には、こちらでは｜対応[たいおう]しかねます。

synonyms.note: がたい also means 'hard to do' (理解しがたい), often about judgment or emotion; かねる leans toward being unable to, and to polite refusals.

related.note: かねない is the negation of かねる but has shifted to mean 'might well (do something bad)' rather than 'be unable to'.
にくい describes something being physically hard to do (書きにくい); かねる is more about inability or reluctance in a situation.

title: かのように・かのようだ
kana: かのように・かのようだ
romaji: ka no you ni / ka no you da
meaning: as if; as though (when it is actually not so)
summary: [plain form] + かのように / かのようだ compares a situation to something it is not really — 'as if'. It is stronger and more literary than plain ようだ, and stresses that the likeness is contrary to fact. かのように modifies a following verb or clause; かのようだ ends the sentence.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ かのように／かのようだ
Noun／な-adjective ＋ である ＋ かのように／かのようだ
pitfalls: It implies the likeness is not real (he acts as if he knew, but he didn't); plain ようだ can state a genuine inference.
With a noun, insert である: 専門家であるかのように, not 専門家かのように.

examples.ja: 彼は何も知らなかったかのように、平然としていた。
examples.en: He stayed perfectly calm, as if he had known nothing at all.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜何[なに]も｜知[し]らなかったかのように、｜平然[へいぜん]としていた。

examples.ja: その部屋は、何年も人が住んでいなかったかのように静まり返っていた。
examples.en: The room was utterly silent, as though no one had lived there for years.
examples.f: その｜部屋[へや]は、｜何[なん]｜年[ねん]も｜人[ひと]が｜住[す]んでいなかったかのように｜静まり返[しずまりかえ]っていた。

synonyms.note: まるで pairs with ようだ for 'just as if'; かのように carries the same figurative sense but is more literary and does not need まるで.
ようだ states a likeness or inference that may well be true; かのように adds the sense that it is not actually so.

related.note: みたいだ is the casual 'like / as if'; かのように is the formal, written counterpart with a contrary-to-fact nuance.

title: からして
meaning: even (starting with); judging from
summary: からして has two related uses. After a noun it means 'even ~ / starting with ~': it picks one representative example to imply that the rest is the same — 態度からして = 'even his attitude, to begin with'. It can also mean 'judging from', presenting grounds for an evaluation.
pitfalls: In the 'even ~' use, the noun is a first, representative example implying the whole, and the following clause is usually an evaluation.
The 'even/starting with' sense often carries a critical or emphatic tone about the example chosen.

examples.ja: あの店は、店員の態度からして感じが悪い。
examples.en: At that shop, even the staff's attitude, for a start, is unpleasant.
examples.f: あの｜店[みせ]は、｜店員[てんいん]の｜態度[たいど]からして｜感[かん]じが｜悪[わる]い。

examples.ja: 名前からして、この料理は外国のものだと分かる。
examples.en: Just from the name, you can tell this dish is a foreign one.
examples.f: ｜名前[なまえ]からして、この｜料理[りょうり]は｜外国[がいこく]のものだと｜分[わ]かる。

synonyms.note: からすると / からすれば covers the 'judging from' sense; からして adds the distinct 'even (to begin with)' use that からすると lacks.

related.note: さえ also highlights an extreme example ('even ~'); からして presents its example as a starting point that implies the rest.

title: からすると・からすれば
kana: からすると・からすれば
meaning: judging from; from the standpoint of; considering
summary: Noun + からすると / からすれば presents the basis or standpoint of a judgment — 'going by X' or 'from X's point of view'. It may take a piece of evidence (この様子からすると) or a person's perspective (親からすれば), and the main clause states the conclusion drawn from it.
structure: Noun ＋ からすると／からすれば
pitfalls: It marks the grounds or viewpoint of an inference; the main clause is the conclusion, so it usually ends in a judgment (〜だろう、〜に違いない).
With a person, it gives that person's perspective, not necessarily the speaker's own opinion.

examples.ja: あの慌てぶりからすると、何か問題が起きたに違いない。
examples.en: Judging from how flustered he is, something must have gone wrong.
examples.f: あの｜慌[あわ]てぶりからすると、｜何[なに]か｜問題[もんだい]が｜起[お]きたに｜違[ちが]いない。

examples.ja: 親からすれば、子どもはいくつになっても心配なものだ。
examples.en: From a parent's point of view, you worry about your children no matter how old they get.
examples.f: ｜親[おや]からすれば、｜子[こ]どもはいくつになっても｜心配[しんぱい]なものだ。

synonyms.note: から見ると frames the same idea as a viewpoint one 'looks from'; からすると is essentially interchangeable in the 'judging from' sense.
からして also means 'judging from', but additionally has an 'even (to begin with)' use that からすると does not.

related.note: によると cites a source of information ('according to'); からすると draws the speaker's own inference from evidence or a standpoint.

title: からといって
meaning: just because ~ (it doesn't mean); simply because
summary: [plain form] + からといって introduces a reason that one might expect to justify a certain conclusion, and then rejects that conclusion: 'just because X, it does not follow that Y'. It is almost always paired with a negative or limiting ending such as わけではない or とは限らない.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ からといって
pitfalls: It is typically followed by a negative/limiting statement (〜とは限らない、〜わけではない); it exists to reject an over-hasty conclusion.
The reason it raises is real; what it denies is only the assumed conclusion drawn from it.

examples.ja: 都会に住んでいるからといって、みんなが生活に満足しているわけではない。
examples.en: Just because someone lives in the city doesn't mean everyone is satisfied with their life.
examples.f: ｜都会[とかい]に｜住[す]んでいるからといって、みんなが｜生活[せいかつ]に｜満足[まんぞく]しているわけではない。

examples.ja: 安いからといって、質が悪いとは限らない。
examples.en: Just because it's cheap doesn't necessarily mean the quality is poor.
examples.f: ｜安[やす]いからといって、｜質[しつ]が｜悪[わる]いとは｜限[かぎ]らない。

related.note: というわけではない is the denial half ('it's not that ~'), which からといって often leads into.
必ずしも ('not necessarily') frequently appears in the concluding clause paired with からといって.

title: からには
meaning: now that; since; given that (so one should ~)
summary: [plain form] + からには means 'now that / since X is the case', and because it is so, the speaker draws a firm consequence: the main clause states a resolve, an obligation, or a natural expectation (should, must, of course). It commits the speaker more strongly than a plain から.
structure: Noun／な-adjective ＋ である ＋ からには
pitfalls: The main clause usually expresses determination or obligation (〜べきだ、〜つもりだ、〜なければならない), not a neutral fact.
It presents X as a settled premise; use it when a decision or situation is already fixed, not for a mere hypothesis.

examples.ja: 引き受けたからには、最後まで責任を持ってやり遂げます。
examples.en: Now that I've taken it on, I will see it through to the end and take full responsibility.
examples.f: ｜引き受[ひきう]けたからには、｜最後[さいご]まで｜責任[せきにん]を｜持[も]ってやり｜遂[と]げます。

examples.ja: 試合に出るからには、優勝を目指したい。
examples.en: Since I'm going to take part in the match, I want to aim for the championship.
examples.f: ｜試合[しあい]に｜出[で]るからには、｜優勝[ゆうしょう]を｜目指[めざ]したい。

synonyms.note: 以上は means much the same 'now that / since', and is nearly interchangeable; からには sounds a touch more conversational.
上は also means 'now that', but is more formal and written; からには is the everyday choice.

related.note: Plain から just gives a reason; からには adds that, given the premise, a matching resolve or obligation follows.

title: から見ると
meaning: from the viewpoint of; seen from; judging from
summary: Noun + から見ると / から見れば / から見て takes a standpoint or a body of evidence and states how things appear from there — 'seen from X's perspective' or 'judging by X'. 見る ('to look') frames a point of view, whether a person's perspective or the grounds for a judgment.
structure: Noun ＋ から見ると／から見れば／から見て
pitfalls: It marks the perspective or evidence a judgment rests on; it is not used for physically 'looking out from' a place.
The main clause reports how something looks from that standpoint, so it usually ends in an assessment.

examples.ja: 大人から見ると、子どものけんかはささいなことだ。
examples.en: Seen from an adult's perspective, children's quarrels are trivial matters.
examples.f: ｜大人[おとな]から｜見[み]ると、｜子[こ]どものけんかはささいなことだ。

examples.ja: この成績から見ると、彼は合格する可能性が高い。
examples.en: Judging from these grades, he has a high chance of passing.
examples.f: この｜成績[せいせき]から｜見[み]ると、｜彼[かれ]は｜合格[ごうかく]する｜可能[かのう]｜性[せい]が｜高[たか]い。

synonyms.note: からすると / からすれば expresses the same 'judging from / from the standpoint of' with little difference in meaning.
からして shares the 'judging from' sense but also has a separate 'even (to begin with)' use.

related.note: にとって marks whom or what something matters to ('for ~'); から見ると frames the viewpoint from which a judgment is made.

title: 気
meaning: 気 expressions: mind, feeling, inclination (気がする, 気になる, 気にする, and more)
summary: 気 ('mind, spirit, feeling') forms a large family of set expressions about one's mental state: 気がする (have a feeling), 気になる (be bothered or curious), 気にする (mind, worry about), 気をつける (be careful), 気が済む (feel satisfied). The noun 気 combines with a fixed particle and verb in each idiom to describe feelings and inclinations.
pitfalls: 気になる is spontaneous (something bothers you); 気にする is deliberate (you choose to worry) — same 気, different verb.
Each idiom fixes its particle (気がする, 気をつける, 気が済む); you cannot swap them freely.

examples.ja: どこかで彼に会ったような気がする。
examples.en: I have a feeling I've met him somewhere before.
examples.f: どこかで｜彼[かれ]に｜会[あ]ったような｜気[き]がする。

examples.ja: 小さなことは気にしないほうがいい。
examples.en: It's better not to worry about the little things.
examples.f: ｜小[ちい]さなことは｜気[き]にしないほうがいい。

related.note: が気になる is one specific member: something weighs on your mind or draws your curiosity.
ような気がする is the fixed pattern 'have a feeling that ~', built from 気がする.
に気をつける ('be careful about ~') is another everyday idiom in the 気 family.

title: 逆に
meaning: conversely; on the contrary; if anything, the opposite
summary: 逆に is an adverb meaning 'the other way around / conversely'. It flags that what follows runs counter to what was just said or to what you would expect — you tried for one result and got the reverse, or you turn to look at the opposite case. 励ますつもりが逆に怒らせた = meant to encourage, but instead made them angry.
pitfalls: 逆に signals a reversal or the opposite case; it is not a neutral 'also / next'.
It often introduces an outcome that is the reverse of what you intended or expected, so the two halves clash.

examples.ja: 彼を励ますつもりだったが、逆に怒らせてしまった。
examples.en: I meant to encourage him, but instead I ended up making him angry.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]を｜励[はげ]ますつもりだったが、｜逆[ぎゃく]に｜怒[おこ]らせてしまった。

examples.ja: 値段が高ければいいとは限らない。逆に、安い方が質のいい場合もある。
examples.en: A high price doesn't always mean good quality. On the contrary, there are cases where the cheaper option is better made.
examples.f: ｜値段[ねだん]が｜高[たか]ければいいとは｜限[かぎ]らない。｜逆[ぎゃく]に、｜安[やす]い｜方[ほう]が｜質[しつ]のいい｜場合[ばあい]もある。

synonyms.note: かえって stresses a result contrary to what you'd hope for; 逆に more broadly presents the reverse side or opposite case.
反面 weighs the other side of the same thing; 逆に marks a straight reversal or contrary outcome.

related.note: 一方で lays out the other of two coexisting sides neutrally; 逆に emphasizes that the second point overturns the first.

title: 〜強
meaning: a little more than; just over (suffix on a quantity)
summary: Placed right after a number or amount, 〜強 means 'a bit more than that figure'. It rounds down to a round number and signals that the true value sits slightly above it — 二年強 = just over two years, 五割強 = a little over 50%. Common in statistics, reports, and news.
pitfalls: Here 強 reads きょう and means 'and a bit more'; it has nothing to do with 強い ('strong').
It marks a value just above the stated figure; the mirror suffix for 'a little less' is 〜弱.

examples.ja: この工事には二年強かかった。
examples.en: This construction took just over two years.
examples.f: この｜工事[こうじ]には｜二[に]｜年[ねん]｜強[きょう]かかった。

examples.ja: 会場には千人強の観客が集まった。
examples.en: A little over a thousand spectators gathered at the venue.
examples.f: ｜会場[かいじょう]には｜千[せん]｜人[にん]｜強[きょう]の｜観客[かんきゃく]が｜集[あつ]まった。

antonyms.note: 〜弱 is the mirror suffix, marking a value slightly below the stated figure.

related.note: 以上 means 'that amount or more' inclusively; 〜強 means a bit above a rounded-down figure.

title: くせして
meaning: even though; and yet (with blame or scorn)
summary: くせして is a colloquial, blunter variant of くせに. It joins two clauses where the second clashes with what the first would lead you to expect, and it carries criticism, contempt, or complaint aimed at the subject — 知っているくせして教えてくれない = knows it, and yet won't tell me. Normally used about someone else, not oneself.
structure: な-adjective ＋ な ＋ くせして
pitfalls: It carries a critical, faultfinding tone; for neutral concession use のに instead.
It normally judges another person's behavior, so it sounds odd applied to yourself.
Same meaning as くせに, just more colloquial and often harsher.

examples.ja: 自分では何もやらないくせして、文句ばかり言っている。
examples.en: He never does anything himself, and yet all he does is complain.
examples.f: ｜自分[じぶん]では｜何[なに]もやらないくせして、｜文句[もんく]ばかり｜言[い]っている。

examples.ja: 本当は寂しいくせして、平気なふりをしている。
examples.en: Deep down she's lonely, and yet she keeps pretending she's fine.
examples.f: ｜本当[ほんとう]は｜寂[さび]しいくせして、｜平気[へいき]なふりをしている。

synonyms.note: くせに is the same critical 'even though'; くせして is the more colloquial, often blunter form.

related.note: ながらも is a literary concessive 'although' with no scorn; くせして adds blame or contempt.

title: 〜げ
meaning: looking ~; with an air of ~ (seeming)
summary: 〜げ attaches to an adjective stem, or to the stem of 〜たい, to form a な-adjective/adverb meaning 'looking ~, with an air of ~'. 寂しげ = looking lonely, 自慢げ = with a boastful air, 言いたげ = as if wanting to say something. It describes the outward impression a person gives off, usually about their feelings.
pitfalls: Drop the final い of an い-adjective: 寂しい → 寂しげ, not 寂しいげ.
It reports an outward impression the person seems to give, not a firm claim about their true feelings.
It attaches only to a limited set of feeling/appearance words; you can't append it freely to any adjective.

examples.ja: 彼女は何か言いたげな表情でこちらを見ていた。
examples.en: She was looking my way with an expression as if she wanted to say something.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜何[なに]か｜言[い]いたげな｜表情[ひょうじょう]でこちらを｜見[み]ていた。

examples.ja: 子供たちは自慢げに賞状を見せてくれた。
examples.en: The children showed me their certificates with an air of pride.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]たちは｜自慢[じまん]げに｜賞状[しょうじょう]を｜見[み]せてくれた。

synonyms.note: そうな reports how something looks generally; 〜げ centers on the air a person gives off, especially about feelings.
っぽい says something has a ~ quality or tendency; 〜げ is specifically 'seeming / looking'.

title: 傾向がある
meaning: there is a tendency to; tend to
summary: 傾向がある states that something tends to happen or that people tend to act a certain way. 傾向 is 'inclination / trend', so the phrase describes a general, often statistical pattern rather than a one-time event — 若者は新聞を読まない傾向がある = young people tend not to read newspapers. Common in analytical and written Japanese.
structure: Verb［dictionary form／ない form］＋ 傾向がある
Noun ＋ の ＋ 傾向がある
pitfalls: It describes a broad, general tendency, so avoid it for a single occasion.
Attach it to the plain verb and negate the verb itself (減らない傾向がある), rather than negating the whole phrase.

examples.ja: 近年、結婚する年齢が上がる傾向がある。
examples.en: In recent years, the age at which people marry has tended to rise.
examples.f: ｜近年[きんねん]、｜結婚[けっこん]する｜年齢[ねんれい]が｜上[あ]がる｜傾向[けいこう]がある。

examples.ja: 彼は物事を悪い方に考える傾向がある。
examples.en: He tends to think about things in the worst way.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜物事[ものごと]を｜悪[わる]い｜方[ほう]に｜考[かんが]える｜傾向[けいこう]がある。

synonyms.note: がち is a colloquial 'tend to / prone to', usually negative; 傾向がある is neutral and more formal.
嫌いがある is a literary 'has a bad tendency to' and is always negative; 傾向がある can be neutral.

title: ことだから
meaning: since it's ~ (given what we know of them); knowing ~
summary: 〜ことだから builds a prediction on the known character of a person or group. Because we know what they are like, we can guess how they will act — 几帳面な彼のことだから遅れないだろう = knowing how punctual he is, he surely won't be late. It attaches to a noun (usually a person) + の.
structure: Noun［person／group］＋ の ＋ ことだから
pitfalls: The noun is normally a specific person or group you both know; the guess leans on their established character.
It sets up a prediction about that person's behavior, so it usually leads into だろう・にちがいない, not a plain statement of fact.

examples.ja: しっかり者の彼女のことだから、準備は完璧だろう。
examples.en: Knowing how dependable she is, her preparations are surely perfect.
examples.f: しっかり｜者[しゃ]の｜彼女[かのじょ]のことだから、｜準備[じゅんび]は｜完璧[かんぺき]だろう。

examples.ja: 約束を守る田中さんのことだから、きっと来てくれるはずだ。
examples.en: Since it's Tanaka, who always keeps his word, I'm sure he'll come.
examples.f: ｜約束[やくそく]を｜守[まも]る｜田中[たなか]さんのことだから、きっと｜来[き]てくれるはずだ。

related.note: だけに draws a heightened result from a known fact ('all the more because'); ことだから predicts behavior from someone's character.
こともあって states a contributing reason ('partly because'); ことだから predicts an action from what someone is like.

title: ことなく
meaning: without ~ing; never once ~ing
summary: 〜ことなく attaches to a dictionary-form verb to mean 'without doing that action' — 休むことなく働いた = worked without resting. It is the more formal, written counterpart of 〜ないで／〜ずに, and often stresses that something carried on the whole time without that action ever interrupting it.
pitfalls: Attach it to the dictionary form (止まることなく), not the ない form.
It belongs to formal or written Japanese; in speech 〜ないで or 〜ずに is more natural.

examples.ja: 彼は最後まで諦めることなく、走り続けた。
examples.en: He kept running to the very end without ever giving up.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜最後[さいご]まで｜諦[あきら]めることなく、｜走[はし]り｜続[つづ]けた。

examples.ja: この工場は三十年間、一度も止まることなく稼働している。
examples.en: This factory has run for thirty years without stopping even once.
examples.f: この｜工場[こうじょう]は｜三[さん]｜十[じゅう]｜年間[ねんかん]、｜一[いち]｜度[ど]も｜止[と]まることなく｜稼働[かどう]している。

synonyms.note: ずに also means 'without doing'; ことなく is more formal and often more emphatic about continuity.
なしに attaches to a noun ('without ~'); ことなく attaches to a verb ('without doing ~').

title: ことにはならない
meaning: it doesn't (automatically) mean that ~; that doesn't make it ~
summary: 〜ことにはならない rejects a conclusion someone might jump to — 'that doesn't mean ~'. It commonly follows からといって: 高いからといって、いい物だということにはならない = just because it's expensive doesn't make it a good product. It refuses to treat one fact as if it settled another.
structure: Verb／Sentence［plain form］＋ ことにはならない
Noun ＋ という ＋ ことにはならない
pitfalls: It denies an inference ('doesn't mean'), not a fact ('didn't happen').
It is very often set up by からといって earlier in the sentence.

examples.ja: 謝ったからといって、すべてが許されることにはならない。
examples.en: Just because you apologized doesn't mean everything is forgiven.
examples.f: ｜謝[あやま]ったからといって、すべてが｜許[ゆる]されることにはならない。

examples.ja: 一度失敗したからといって、才能がないことにはならない。
examples.en: One failure doesn't mean you have no talent.
examples.f: ｜一度[いちど]｜失敗[しっぱい]したからといって、｜才能[さいのう]がないことにはならない。

related.note: からといって sets up the premise ('just because ~'); ことにはならない then denies the conclusion drawn from it.
わけではない broadly denies an implied conclusion; ことにはならない specifically denies that one fact makes another true.

title: 幸い・幸いなことに
kana: さいわい・さいわいなことに
meaning: fortunately; luckily; happily
summary: 幸いなことに (or just 幸い) is a sentence-opening adverb meaning 'fortunately' — it frames the whole sentence as a lucky outcome: 幸い、けが人はいなかった = fortunately, there were no injuries. On its own 幸い can also be a な-adjective/noun meaning 'a blessing / welcome'.
pitfalls: As an opener it comments on the whole sentence, so it sits at the front, not inside the predicate.
幸い alone can also be a な-adjective meaning 'fortunate / welcome' (〜と幸いです = I'd be grateful if ~); the adverbial 'fortunately' sense is 幸い（に）／幸いなことに.

examples.ja: 幸いなことに、事故に遭ったのに誰も怪我をしなかった。
examples.en: Fortunately, although there was an accident, no one was hurt.
examples.f: ｜幸[さいわ]いなことに、｜事故[じこ]に｜遭[あ]ったのに｜誰[だれ]も｜怪我[けが]をしなかった。

examples.ja: 道に迷ったが、幸い親切な人が案内してくれた。
examples.en: I got lost, but luckily a kind person showed me the way.
examples.f: ｜道[みち]に｜迷[まよ]ったが、｜幸[さいわ]い｜親切[しんせつ]な｜人[ひと]が｜案内[あんない]してくれた。

related.note: 〜ことに fronts any emotion ('to my surprise/joy/etc.'); 幸いなことに is one fixed member of that pattern, locked onto 'luckily'.

title: 〜ざる
meaning: not ~ (classical/literary negative, before a noun)
summary: 〜ざる is a classical negative ending equal to 〜ない before a noun. It survives in modern written and set expressions — 絶えざる努力 = ceaseless effort, 予期せざる事態 = an unforeseen situation. It attaches to the ない-form base (the あ-stem) of a verb, with する → せざる and くる → こざる. Mostly literary or fixed-phrase, not everyday speech.
structure: Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋ ざる
する → せざる／くる → こざる
pitfalls: 〜ざる comes before a noun (絶えざる努力); the clause-ending / adverbial form is 〜ず.
Irregular: する becomes せざる, not しざる.
It is literary; in ordinary sentences use 〜ない.

examples.ja: 絶えざる努力の末に、彼は夢をかなえた。
examples.en: After ceaseless effort, he made his dream come true.
examples.f: ｜絶[た]えざる｜努力[どりょく]の｜末[すえ]に、｜彼[かれ]は｜夢[ゆめ]をかなえた。

examples.ja: 予期せざる事態が起きた。
examples.en: An unforeseen situation arose.
examples.f: ｜予期[よき]せざる｜事態[じたい]が｜起[お]きた。

synonyms.note: 〜ぬ is the classical negative that ends a clause or precedes a noun; 〜ざる is a parallel attributive form.

related.note: ざるを得ない ('have no choice but') is built on this same ざる base, fixed with を得ない.

title: ざるを得ない
meaning: have no choice but to ~; cannot help ~ing
summary: 〜ざるを得ない attaches to a verb's ない-form base to say the speaker is forced by circumstances into the action, often reluctantly — 認めざるを得ない = have no choice but to admit it. Formal in tone, with する → せざるを得ない.
structure: Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋ ざるを得ない
する → せざるを得ない
pitfalls: Formed on the ない-base minus ない: 行かない → 行かざるを得ない.
Irregular: する → せざるを得ない, not しざるを得ない.
It conveys reluctant compulsion by outside circumstances, not a free personal choice.

examples.ja: 台風で、旅行を中止せざるを得なかった。
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, we had no choice but to cancel the trip.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]で、｜旅行[りょこう]を｜中止[ちゅうし]せざるを｜得[え]なかった。

examples.ja: これだけ証拠があれば、事実を認めざるを得ない。
examples.en: With this much evidence, I have no choice but to admit the facts.
examples.f: これだけ｜証拠[しょうこ]があれば、｜事実[じじつ]を｜認[みと]めざるを｜得[え]ない。

synonyms.note: よりほかない also means 'nothing to do but'; ざるを得ない stresses reluctant compulsion by circumstance.
ないわけにはいかない is 'can't not do', driven by duty or social obligation; ざるを得ない is driven by unavoidable circumstances.
〜しかない is a plainer, more colloquial 'have no choice but'; ざるを得ない is more formal.

related.note: 〜ざる is the classical negative base on which this fixed pattern is built.

title: しかしながら
meaning: however; nevertheless; that said (formal)
summary: しかしながら is a formal conjunction meaning 'however / nevertheless'. It is a heavier, more written version of しかし, opening a sentence to introduce something that runs against what came before. Common in essays, speeches, and business correspondence.
structure: Sentence。 ＋ しかしながら、 ＋ Sentence
pitfalls: It is markedly formal and written; in conversation しかし or でも is more natural.
It opens a new sentence; it does not join two clauses inside one sentence the way が does.

examples.ja: 計画は順調に進んでいた。しかしながら、予算の問題が生じた。
examples.en: The plan was progressing smoothly. However, a budget problem arose.
examples.f: ｜計画[けいかく]は｜順調[じゅんちょう]に｜進[すす]んでいた。しかしながら、｜予算[よさん]の｜問題[もんだい]が｜生[しょう]じた。

examples.ja: ご提案は理解いたしました。しかしながら、今回は見送らせていただきます。
examples.en: I understand your proposal. That said, we will pass on it this time.
examples.f: ご｜提案[ていあん]は｜理解[りかい]いたしました。しかしながら、｜今回[こんかい]は｜見送[みおく]らせていただきます。

synonyms.note: しかし is the plain 'but / however'; しかしながら is the more formal, written-style version.
けれども can also join clauses inside one sentence; しかしながら only opens a fresh sentence.

related.note: ところが adds surprise ('but then, unexpectedly'); しかしながら is neutral, formal contrast.
したがって is the conclusive formal conjunction ('therefore'); しかしながら is its contrastive counterpart.

title: しかも
meaning: moreover; what's more; and on top of that
summary: しかも adds a further point that reinforces the previous one, usually making it more striking — 'and what's more'. 安くて、しかもおいしい = cheap, and on top of that delicious. The added fact points the same direction as the first (both good, or both bad), heightening the effect.
pitfalls: The second point normally reinforces the first (same positive or same negative direction), unlike 'but'.
Don't confuse it with でも／しかし; しかも adds to the point, it doesn't contradict it.

examples.ja: この店の料理は量が多く、しかも値段が安い。
examples.en: The dishes at this restaurant are generous in portion, and what's more, cheap.
examples.f: この｜店[みせ]の｜料理[りょうり]は｜量[りょう]が｜多[おお]く、しかも｜値段[ねだん]が｜安[やす]い。

examples.ja: 彼は遅刻し、しかも謝りもしなかった。
examples.en: He was late, and on top of that he didn't even apologize.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜遅刻[ちこく]し、しかも｜謝[あやま]りもしなかった。

synonyms.note: その上 is a very close 'on top of that'; しかも can feel a touch more emphatic.
〜上に attaches within a clause ('in addition to ~ing'); しかも links whole sentences.
ばかりか is 'not only ~ but even ~', with escalation to a surprising point; しかも simply piles on a reinforcing fact.

title: 次第だ・次第で
meaning: depending on ~; determined by ~
summary: Noun＋次第だ／次第で means the outcome hinges entirely on that noun — 'it all depends on ~'. 成功は君の努力次第だ = success depends on your effort. 次第で before a clause means 'depending on ~, ...'. It points to the deciding factor behind a result.
pitfalls: It attaches straight to a noun (天気次第だ), with no の or particle in between.
This 次第 means 'depending on'; the 〜次第 after a verb stem ('as soon as ~') and the adverb 次第に ('gradually') are different uses.

examples.ja: 明日出かけるかどうかは、天気次第だ。
examples.en: Whether we go out tomorrow depends on the weather.
examples.f: ｜明日[あした]｜出[で]かけるかどうかは、｜天気[てんき]｜次第[しだい]だ。

examples.ja: 考え方次第で、同じ出来事も違って見える。
examples.en: Depending on how you look at it, the same event can appear different.
examples.f: ｜考え方[かんがえかた]｜次第[しだい]で、｜同[おな]じ｜出来事[できごと]も｜違[ちが]って｜見[み]える。

synonyms.note: によって also means 'depending on / according to'; 次第で focuses on the single factor that decides an outcome.

related.note: 次第に uses the same kanji but is an adverb meaning 'gradually'; a different function entirely.

title: 次第に
meaning: gradually; by degrees; steadily
summary: 次第に is an adverb meaning 'gradually, little by little'. It describes a change that unfolds step by step — 空が次第に暗くなった = the sky gradually darkened. It is a somewhat formal, written-flavored synonym of だんだん.
pitfalls: It describes a gradual change over time, so it pairs with verbs of becoming/changing, not one-off actions.
It is more formal than だんだん and suits writing and narration.
Don't confuse it with 次第だ／次第で ('depending on'), which attaches to a noun.

examples.ja: 日が暮れて、あたりは次第に静かになった。
examples.en: As the sun set, the surroundings gradually grew quiet.
examples.f: ｜日[ひ]が｜暮[く]れて、あたりは｜次第[しだい]に｜静[しず]かになった。

examples.ja: 練習を重ねるうちに、彼の技術は次第に上達した。
examples.en: As he kept practicing, his skills gradually improved.
examples.f: ｜練習[れんしゅう]を｜重[かさ]ねるうちに、｜彼[かれ]の｜技術[ぎじゅつ]は｜次第[しだい]に｜上達[じょうたつ]した。

synonyms.note: だんだん is the everyday 'gradually'; 次第に is more formal and written.
つつある is 'in the process of ~ing', framing an ongoing change; 次第に is an adverb describing how the change proceeds.

related.note: 次第で shares the kanji but means 'depending on', attaching to a noun; 次第に is 'gradually'.

title: したがって
meaning: therefore; consequently; accordingly (formal)
summary: したがって is a formal conjunction that draws a logical conclusion from what precedes — 'therefore, accordingly'. 需要が増えた。したがって、価格も上がった = demand rose; therefore prices went up too. Common in academic and business writing.
pitfalls: It is written and formal; in speech だから or それで is more natural.
Here it is a conjunction meaning 'therefore'; the homophone 〜にしたがって ('as ~ / in accordance with ~') is a separate pattern.

examples.ja: この地域は降水量が少ない。したがって、農業には向いていない。
examples.en: This region gets little precipitation. Therefore, it is not suited to agriculture.
examples.f: この｜地域[ちいき]は｜降水[こうすい]｜量[りょう]が｜少[すく]ない。したがって、｜農業[のうぎょう]には｜向[む]いていない。

examples.ja: 会員以外は入れません。したがって、事前の登録が必要です。
examples.en: Non-members cannot enter. Accordingly, prior registration is required.
examples.f: ｜会員[かいいん]｜以外[いがい]は｜入[い]れません。したがって、｜事前[じぜん]の｜登録[とうろく]が｜必要[ひつよう]です。

synonyms.note: ゆえに is an even more literary 'therefore'; したがって is standard formal register.

related.note: しかしながら is the formal contrastive conjunction ('however'); したがって is its conclusive counterpart.

title: 〜弱
meaning: a little less than; just under (suffix on a quantity)
summary: Placed after a number, 〜弱 means 'a bit less than that figure'. It rounds up to a round number and signals that the true value sits slightly below it — 三千円弱 = just under 3,000 yen, 三割弱 = a little under 30%. Common in statistics and reports; its mirror is 〜強.
pitfalls: Here 弱 reads じゃく and means 'and a bit less'; it has nothing to do with 弱い ('weak').
The opposite, 'a little more than', is 〜強.

examples.ja: この本は二千円弱で買えた。
examples.en: I was able to buy this book for a little under 2,000 yen.
examples.f: この｜本[ほん]は｜二[に]｜千[せん]｜円[えん]｜弱[じゃく]で｜買[か]えた。

examples.ja: 会場には五百人弱が集まった。
examples.en: A little under five hundred people gathered at the venue.
examples.f: ｜会場[かいじょう]には｜五[ご]｜百[ひゃく]｜人[にん]｜弱[じゃく]が｜集[あつ]まった。

antonyms.note: 〜強 is the mirror suffix, marking a value slightly above the stated figure.

title: 〜上
meaning: from the standpoint of ~; in terms of ~; for ~ reasons
summary: Noun＋上 (じょう) means 'from the standpoint of ~ / in terms of ~' — 法律上 = legally, 健康上 = for health reasons, 立場上 = given one's position. It frames the following statement within that particular domain or consideration. It attaches to a limited set of abstract nouns.
pitfalls: This 上 reads じょう and means 'in terms of ~'; it is not うえ ('on top of / after').
It attaches only to a restricted set of abstract nouns (歴史上, 経験上, 教育上); you can't append it to any noun freely.

examples.ja: その計画は予算上、実現が難しい。
examples.en: That plan is hard to realize in budgetary terms.
examples.f: その｜計画[けいかく]は｜予算[よさん]｜上[じょう]、｜実現[じつげん]が｜難[むずか]しい。

examples.ja: 立場上、私からは何も申し上げられません。
examples.en: Given my position, there is nothing I can say.
examples.f: ｜立場[たちば]｜上[じょう]、｜私[わたし]からは｜何[なに]も｜申し上[もうしあ]げられません。

synonyms.note: 的 turns a noun into '~-wise / in terms of ~' broadly; 〜上 is limited to fixed nouns and often means 'from the standpoint of'.

related.note: 上で reads うえで and means 'upon doing / in the course of'; the same kanji, but a different reading and meaning.

title: 少なくとも
meaning: at least; at the very least
summary: 少なくとも means 'at least' — it states a guaranteed minimum, whether a quantity (少なくとも三千円はかかる = it will cost at least 3,000 yen) or a minimal claim you are sure of (少なくとも彼は嘘をつかない = at least he doesn't lie). It marks the floor below which things won't go.
pitfalls: It gives a minimum you are certain of; for a hoped-for minimum ('at least ~, if nothing else') せめて fits better.
With a number it means 'that number or more', marking the lower bound.

examples.ja: この作業には、少なくとも二週間はかかるだろう。
examples.en: This task will probably take at least two weeks.
examples.f: この｜作業[さぎょう]には、｜少[すく]なくとも｜二[に]｜週間[しゅうかん]はかかるだろう。

examples.ja: 全員が賛成ではないが、少なくとも反対する人はいなかった。
examples.en: Not everyone was in favor, but at least there was no one against it.
examples.f: ｜全員[ぜんいん]が｜賛成[さんせい]ではないが、｜少[すく]なくとも｜反対[はんたい]する｜人[ひと]はいなかった。

synonyms.note: せめて expresses a wish for a bare minimum ('at least ~, if nothing else'); 少なくとも states a factual minimum.

related.note: 以上 marks '~ or more' as a suffix on a quantity; 少なくとも is an adverb setting the same lower bound.

title: ずに済む
meaning: to get by without having to do; to be spared doing
summary: ずに済む attaches the classical negative ず to a verb to say that some troublesome action turned out to be unnecessary — the situation was settled without it. The nuance is relief that an unwanted effort, expense, or bother was avoided. する becomes せずに済む.
structure: Verb［ない-form, minus ない］ ＋ ずに済む （する → せずに済む）
pitfalls: する becomes せず, not しず: 電話せずに済む.
It says the action turned out unnecessary (a fortunate avoidance), not merely that you chose not to do it; for a plain 'without doing', use ずに or ないで on their own.

examples.ja: 友達がお金を貸してくれたので、親に頼まずに済んだ。
examples.en: A friend lent me money, so I got by without having to ask my parents.
examples.f: ｜友達[ともだち]がお｜金[かね]を｜貸[か]してくれたので、｜親[おや]に｜頼[たの]まずに｜済[す]んだ。

examples.ja: 電車が動いていたので、歩いて帰らずに済んだ。
examples.en: The trains were running, so I was spared having to walk home.
examples.f: ｜電車[でんしゃ]が｜動[うご]いていたので、｜歩[ある]いて｜帰[かえ]らずに｜済[す]んだ。

synonyms.note: て済む says a matter is settled by doing/being something; ずに済む is the negative side — settled without having to do it.

related.note: ずに plainly means 'without doing', with no sense of avoided trouble; ずに済む adds the relief that the action proved unnecessary.
ないで is the colloquial 'without doing'; ずに済む specifically frames it as escaping an unwanted task.

title: せいか
meaning: perhaps because; maybe owing to
summary: せいか marks a cause the speaker suspects but is not certain of — せい names a cause and か adds 'perhaps'. It is often used for an unexpected or unwelcome result whose reason is only a guess: 年のせいか = 'maybe because of my age'. The tone is tentative rather than assertive.
pitfalls: A noun takes の (寒さのせいか) and a な-adjective takes な before せいか.
Unlike せいで, which states the cause as a fact, せいか only guesses at it — it usually accompanies a tentative statement.

examples.ja: 疲れていたせいか、話の内容をよく覚えていない。
examples.en: Perhaps because I was tired, I don't remember the content of the talk very well.
examples.f: ｜疲[つか]れていたせいか、｜話[はなし]の｜内容[ないよう]をよく｜覚[おぼ]えていない。

examples.ja: 天気が悪かったせいか、来場者はいつもより少なかった。
examples.en: Maybe because the weather was bad, there were fewer visitors than usual.
examples.f: ｜天気[てんき]が｜悪[わる]かったせいか、｜来場[らいじょう]｜者[しゃ]はいつもより｜少[すく]なかった。

synonyms.note: せいで states the (usually negative) cause as a definite fact; せいか only suspects it.

related.note: おかげで credits a good result to a cause; せいか is neutral-to-negative and merely tentative.
ために plainly states 'because of', with no doubt or blame; せいか adds uncertainty.

title: せめて
meaning: at least; at the very least (as a modest wish)
summary: せめて expresses a small minimum the speaker hopes for when the ideal is out of reach — 'if nothing else, at least this much'. Because it voices a wish or request, it typically pairs with a desiderative or volitional ending such as 〜たい, 〜てほしい, or 〜よう.
structure: せめて ＋ Noun／amount ＋ （でも／だけでも）
pitfalls: せめて states a hoped-for minimum, so it leans on a wish or request (〜たい, 〜てほしい); for a plain factual minimum, use 少なくとも instead.

examples.ja: 全部は無理でも、せめて半分だけでも終わらせておきたい。
examples.en: Even if all of it is impossible, I'd at least like to get half of it done.
examples.f: ｜全部[ぜんぶ]は｜無理[むり]でも、せめて｜半分[はんぶん]だけでも｜終[お]わらせておきたい。

examples.ja: 忙しいのは分かるが、せめて連絡くらいはしてほしかった。
examples.en: I know you're busy, but I wish you'd at least gotten in touch.
examples.f: ｜忙[いそが]しいのは｜分[わ]かるが、せめて｜連絡[れんらく]くらいはしてほしかった。

synonyms.note: 少なくとも gives an objective minimum figure; せめて voices a wish for a bare minimum.

related.note: だけましだ accepts a small consolation as already gained; せめて still wishes for the minimum.

title: そういえば
meaning: come to think of it; now that you mention it; speaking of which
summary: そういえば signals that the current topic has just reminded the speaker of something related — it introduces a thought or memory triggered by what was said. Literally 'if you put it that way', it brings up a spontaneous, connected remark.
pitfalls: It links to something just said or noticed; it is not a deliberate topic-changer like ところで, which shifts to an unrelated subject.

examples.ja: そういえば、来週の会議の場所はもう決まったのかな。
examples.en: Come to think of it, has the venue for next week's meeting been decided yet?
examples.f: そういえば、｜来週[らいしゅう]の｜会議[かいぎ]の｜場所[ばしょ]はもう｜決[き]まったのかな。

examples.ja: そういえば、彼から最近何も連絡がないね。
examples.en: Now that you mention it, we haven't heard anything from him lately.
examples.f: そういえば、｜彼[かれ]から｜最近[さいきん]｜何[なに]も｜連絡[れんらく]がないね。

related.note: ところで switches to a fresh, unrelated topic; そういえば follows on from the current one.
ちなみに adds a related side note the speaker offers on purpose; そういえば surfaces something just recalled.

title: その上
meaning: besides; on top of that; furthermore
summary: その上 adds a further point in the same direction as what came before — 'and on top of that'. It stacks an additional, reinforcing fact: good added to good, or bad added to bad. It is a sentence-connecting conjunction.
pitfalls: The added item should point the same way as the first (both favorable or both unfavorable), not contrast with it.

examples.ja: この店は値段が安い。その上、料理の量も多い。
examples.en: This restaurant is cheap. On top of that, the portions are large too.
examples.f: この｜店[みせ]は｜値段[ねだん]が｜安[やす]い。その｜上[うえ]、｜料理[りょうり]の｜量[りょう]も｜多[おお]い。

examples.ja: 道に迷って、その上、財布まで落としてしまった。
examples.en: I got lost, and on top of that, I even dropped my wallet.
examples.f: ｜道[みち]に｜迷[まよ]って、その｜上[うえ]、｜財布[さいふ]まで｜落[お]としてしまった。

synonyms.note: しかも adds an emphatic further point and often sits tighter within the flow; その上 opens a new sentence.

related.note: だけでなく builds 'not only ~ but also' within one sentence; その上 links two full sentences.
ばかりか adds an often surprising further item; その上 is a neutral additive conjunction.
のみならず is a formal written 'not only ~ but also'; その上 is more conversational.

title: それなのに
meaning: and yet; even so; despite that
summary: それなのに opens a sentence to say the result clashes with what the previous statement would lead you to expect — 'and yet, in spite of that'. It carries surprise, dissatisfaction, or complaint about the contradictory outcome.
pitfalls: It joins two separate sentences; within a single sentence, attach のに to the first clause instead.
It often carries a note of complaint or disappointment, not a neutral contrast.

examples.ja: 彼は何度も約束した。それなのに、一度も来なかった。
examples.en: He promised many times. And yet, he never came even once.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜何[なん]｜度[ど]も｜約束[やくそく]した。それなのに、｜一[いち]｜度[ど]も｜来[こ]なかった。

examples.ja: 朝からずっと準備してきた。それなのに、試合は中止になった。
examples.en: I'd been preparing since morning. Despite all that, the match was canceled.
examples.f: ｜朝[あさ]からずっと｜準備[じゅんび]してきた。それなのに、｜試合[しあい]は｜中止[ちゅうし]になった。

synonyms.note: それでも concedes the previous point and pushes on; それなのに reacts with surprise or complaint at the contradiction.

related.note: のに joins the contrast within one sentence; それなのに links two sentences.
にもかかわらず is a formal 'despite'; それなのに is conversational and more emotional.
くせに contrasts with reproach and only about a person; それなのに applies to any situation.

title: それなら
meaning: if that's the case; in that case; then
summary: それなら picks up something just said or established and offers a conclusion or suggestion that follows from it — 'given that, then...'. It responds to a whole situation the other person has raised. In speech it is often shortened to なら or それじゃ.
pitfalls: It responds to an entire situation already stated; the plain conditional なら attaches directly to a word or clause instead.

examples.ja: 「今日は都合が悪いんです。」「それなら、明日にしましょうか。」
examples.en: 'Today doesn't work for me.' 'In that case, shall we make it tomorrow?'
examples.f: 「｜今日[きょう]は｜都合[つごう]が｜悪[わる]いんです。」「それなら、｜明日[あした]にしましょうか。」

examples.ja: 熱があるの？それなら、無理をせずに休んだほうがいい。
examples.en: You have a fever? Then you'd better not push yourself and get some rest.
examples.f: ｜熱[ねつ]があるの？それなら、｜無理[むり]をせずに｜休[やす]んだほうがいい。

synonyms.note: なら is the underlying conditional attached to a word or clause; それなら is 'that being so' as a sentence opener.

title: それにしても
meaning: even so; be that as it may; still
summary: それにしても accepts what was just said but then comments that the degree of something is beyond expectation — often surprise or mild complaint at how extreme it is. 'Even allowing for that, still...'. It keeps the current topic rather than turning to an opposite result.
pitfalls: Unlike それでも ('even so', which pushes to a contrasting result), それにしても stays on the topic and remarks on how it exceeds expectation.

examples.ja: 渋滞は予想していた。それにしても、これほど時間がかかるとは思わなかった。
examples.en: I'd expected traffic. Even so, I never thought it would take this long.
examples.f: ｜渋滞[じゅうたい]は｜予想[よそう]していた。それにしても、これほど｜時間[じかん]がかかるとは｜思[おも]わなかった。

examples.ja: 彼が怒るのは分かる。それにしても、言い方がひどすぎる。
examples.en: I understand that he's angry. Even so, the way he put it was too harsh.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]が｜怒[おこ]るのは｜分[わ]かる。それにしても、｜言い方[いいかた]がひどすぎる。

synonyms.note: それでも concedes and moves to a contrasting result; それにしても comments on an unexpected degree.

related.note: にしても attaches to a word or clause as 'even granting that'; それにしても stands alone at the head of a sentence.
それなのに reacts to a contradiction; それにしても reacts to something exceeding expectation.

title: だけあって
meaning: precisely because; as one would expect of
summary: だけあって introduces a fitting reason for an admirable result — 'being ~, it's no surprise that...'. The speaker praises an outcome as living up to the status, effort, or quality just named, so the result is usually positive and deserved.
structure: Noun／Verb・い-adjective・な-adjective［plain form］ ＋ だけあって ［な-adjective takes な］
pitfalls: The result is presented as a natural, deserved consequence — usually praise; it does not fit purely negative or accidental outcomes.
It normally comments on someone or something other than the speaker's own merit.

examples.ja: さすが有名なホテルだけあって、サービスがすばらしい。
examples.en: As you'd expect of a famous hotel, the service is wonderful.
examples.f: さすが｜有名[ゆうめい]なホテルだけあって、サービスがすばらしい。

examples.ja: 彼女は長年海外に住んでいただけあって、英語がとても自然だ。
examples.en: Precisely because she lived abroad for many years, her English is very natural.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜長年[ながねん]｜海外[かいがい]に｜住[す]んでいただけあって、｜英語[えいご]がとても｜自然[しぜん]だ。

synonyms.note: だけに shares the 'all the more because' sense but can also lead to negative results and stresses the causal link.
だけのことはある ends the sentence as 'it lives up to ~'; だけあって leads into the result mid-sentence.

related.note: さすが marks 'just as expected' and often stands alone; だけあって names the specific reason behind the praise.

title: だけに
meaning: all the more because; being the case, naturally
summary: だけに says that because a condition holds strongly, the result is all the greater or all the more understandable — 'being ~, all the more so'. Unlike だけあって, the outcome can be positive or negative, including heightened disappointment.
structure: Noun／Verb・い-adjective・な-adjective［plain form］ ＋ だけに ［な-adjective takes な］
pitfalls: Distinct from だけあって: だけに freely takes negative or emotional results (期待していただけに、残念だ), where だけあって leans toward deserved praise.

examples.ja: 期待していただけに、結果を聞いてがっかりした。
examples.en: Precisely because I'd had high hopes, I was all the more disappointed to hear the result.
examples.f: ｜期待[きたい]していただけに、｜結果[けっか]を｜聞[き]いてがっかりした。

examples.ja: 彼は長年教師をしていただけに、教え方がとても分かりやすい。
examples.en: Precisely because he was a teacher for many years, his way of teaching is very easy to follow.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜長年[ながねん]｜教師[きょうし]をしていただけに、｜教[おし]え｜方[かた]がとても｜分[わ]かりやすい。

synonyms.note: だけあって is reserved for fitting, usually favorable results; だけに also allows negative or emotional ones.
だけのことはある closes the sentence as 'no wonder'; だけに leads into the result.

related.note: からこそ stresses that this is the sole reason; だけに stresses that the degree of the result matches the cause.

title: だけのことはある
meaning: no wonder; it's not for nothing; it lives up to it
summary: Placed at the end of a sentence, だけのことはある confirms that a result matches the effort, training, or reputation behind it — 'no wonder; it really shows'. It expresses admiration that something has earned its outcome. The shortened 〜だけある is also common.
structure: Verb・い-adjective・な-adjective［plain form］／Noun ＋ だけのことはある
pitfalls: It typically closes the sentence as a comment on a result; だけあって and だけに instead lead into the result mid-sentence.

examples.ja: 毎日練習しているだけのことはある。彼のピアノは本当に上手だ。
examples.en: It's not for nothing that he practices every day — his piano is truly excellent.
examples.f: ｜毎日[まいにち]｜練習[れんしゅう]しているだけのことはある。｜彼[かれ]のピアノは｜本当[ほんとう]に｜上手[じょうず]だ。

examples.ja: この料理は、さすが一流の店だけのことはある。
examples.en: This dish really lives up to the first-class restaurant it comes from.
examples.f: この｜料理[りょうり]は、さすが｜一流[いちりゅう]の｜店[みせ]だけのことはある。

synonyms.note: だけあって leads into the praised result mid-sentence; だけのことはある delivers it as a closing verdict.
だけに means 'all the more because' and can turn negative; だけのことはある is purely admiring approval.

related.note: さすが is a standalone marker of admiration; だけのことはある spells out that the result was earned.

title: だけは
meaning: at least this much; to do all one can of
summary: だけは singles out one thing as a guaranteed minimum — whatever else happens, at least this holds or gets done. A common shape repeats the verb: やるだけはやる = 'do at least all I can'. It stresses that one point, and only that, is assured, often staying non-committal about the outcome.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］ ＋ だけは ＋ （Verb）［same verb repeated］
pitfalls: In the repeated-verb pattern (やるだけはやる), the speaker commits to the effort while leaving the result open.

examples.ja: 合格するかは分からないが、やれるだけはやってみるつもりだ。
examples.en: I don't know whether I'll pass, but I intend to at least do everything I can.
examples.f: ｜合格[ごうかく]するかは｜分[わ]からないが、やれるだけはやってみるつもりだ。

examples.ja: 聞いてもらえないかもしれないが、言うだけは言っておいた。
examples.en: They may not listen, but at least I said what I had to say.
examples.f: ｜聞[き]いてもらえないかもしれないが、｜言[い]うだけは｜言[い]っておいた。
