related.note: にかけて marks a span from one point to another; にかけては marks the field in which someone excels.
において neutrally marks the sphere or setting; にかけては specifically frames it as a strength someone is best at.

title: に決まっている
meaning: surely; of course; it's bound to be
summary: に決まっている voices the speaker's firm personal conviction that something is obviously the case — 'of course it is; it's bound to be'. そんな話うそに決まっている ('that story is obviously a lie'). It is subjective, emphatic, and rather casual, attaching straight to the plain form.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ に決まっている
Noun／な-adjective ＋ に決まっている
pitfalls: It states the speaker's personal conviction ('obviously!'), so it is emphatic and casual — weaker in objective or formal writing than に違いない or に相違ない.
Attach directly to the plain form; with nouns and な-adjectives no だ appears: 便利に決まっている, not 便利だに決まっている.

examples.ja: あんなに練習したのだから、彼が勝つに決まっています。
examples.en: He practiced that much, so of course he'll win.
examples.f: あんなに｜練習[れんしゅう]したのだから、｜彼[かれ]が｜勝[か]つに｜決[き]まっています。

examples.ja: こんな時間に電話しても、みんな寝ているに決まっている。
examples.en: Calling at an hour like this — everyone's obviously asleep.
examples.f: こんな｜時間[じかん]に｜電話[でんわ]しても、みんな｜寝[ね]ているに｜決[き]まっている。

synonyms.note: に違いない is a more measured 'must be' based on reasoning; に決まっている is a blunter, more emotional 'obviously'.
に相違ない is the formal, written 'without a doubt'; に決まっている is its casual, conversational cousin.

related.note: はずだ is a reasoned expectation that can be revised; に決まっている is a stubborn conviction that brooks no doubt.

title: に気をつける
meaning: to be careful about; to watch out for
summary: 〜に気をつける marks the thing you should watch out for or take care of. The target takes に: 足元に気をつける ('watch your step'), 健康に気をつける ('take care of your health'). It expresses ongoing caution or attention directed at that thing.
pitfalls: The thing you watch out for takes に, not を: 車に気をつける, not 車を気をつける.
〜に気をつける is 'be careful about' (ongoing caution); the similar-sounding 〜に気がつく means 'to notice / realize' — a different meaning.

examples.ja: 階段は暗いので、足元に気をつけてください。
examples.en: The stairs are dark, so please watch your step.
examples.f: ｜階段[かいだん]は｜暗[くら]いので、｜足元[あしもと]に｜気[き]をつけてください。

examples.ja: 季節の変わり目は、体調に気をつけたほうがいいですよ。
examples.en: At the change of seasons, you'd better take care of your health.
examples.f: ｜季節[きせつ]の｜変わり目[かわりめ]は、｜体調[たいちょう]に｜気[き]をつけたほうがいいですよ。

related.note: に気がつく is 'to notice/realize' something (an involuntary discovery); に気をつける is 'to be careful about' something on purpose.

title: に加えて
meaning: in addition to; on top of
summary: Noun＋に加えて stacks one thing on top of another — 家賃に加えて光熱費も ('on top of rent, utilities too'). It is a somewhat formal way to add an extra element of the same kind onto an existing base.
structure: Verb／い-adjective／な-adjective［plain form］＋ のに加えて
pitfalls: It attaches to a noun; to add a whole clause, nominalize with の — 忙しいのに加えて ('on top of being busy').
It quietly stacks a like item onto a base; unlike だけでなく it doesn't carry the 'not only ~ but even (surprisingly)' punch.

examples.ja: この地域は交通が便利なことに加えて、家賃も安い。
examples.en: This area has convenient transport, and on top of that the rent is cheap.
examples.f: この｜地域[ちいき]は｜交通[こうつう]が｜便利[べんり]なことに｜加[くわ]えて、｜家賃[やちん]も｜安[やす]い。

examples.ja: 強い風に加えて気温も下がり、外はとても寒くなった。
examples.en: In addition to the strong wind, the temperature dropped, and it got very cold outside.
examples.f: ｜強[つよ]い｜風[かぜ]に｜加[くわ]えて｜気温[きおん]も｜下[さ]がり、｜外[そと]はとても｜寒[さむ]くなった。

synonyms.note: 上に also piles one thing onto another and works after clauses too; に加えて is a touch more formal and noun-based.
だけでなく leans on a 'not only ~ but also' contrast; に加えて neutrally adds one item to another.

related.note: ばかりか adds a further, often stronger point ('not only ~ but even'); に加えて simply totals up two elements.

title: に越したことはない
meaning: there's nothing better than; it's best to ~
summary: に越したことはない says a certain state is the ideal one to have, even if not strictly required — 用心するに越したことはない ('you can't go wrong being cautious'). It gently recommends the best option while allowing that the less-ideal alternative is still acceptable.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ に越したことはない
い-adjective ＋ に越したことはない
Noun／な-adjective ＋（である）＋ に越したことはない
pitfalls: The nuance is 'it would be best / can't hurt', not a strict obligation — the less-ideal option still counts as fine.
It predicts a preference, so it pairs naturally with もし／〜なら ('if possible, it's best to…').

examples.ja: 旅行の予約は、早めにするに越したことはありません。
examples.en: When it comes to travel bookings, there's nothing better than doing it early.
examples.f: ｜旅行[りょこう]の｜予約[よやく]は、｜早[はや]めにするに｜越[こ]したことはありません。

examples.ja: 家から近いに越したことはないが、家賃も考える必要がある。
examples.en: You can't beat being close to home, but you also have to think about the rent.
examples.f: ｜家[いえ]から｜近[ちか]いに｜越[こ]したことはないが、｜家賃[やちん]も｜考[かんが]える｜必要[ひつよう]がある。

synonyms.note: に限る flatly declares N the best; に越したことはない softly recommends it while leaving room for other options.

related.note: ほうがいい gives a plain 'you'd better'; に越したことはない frames it as 'nothing beats it, though it isn't a must'.

title: に応えて
meaning: in response to; living up to (expectations/demand)
summary: Noun＋に応えて means acting so as to meet or live up to something directed at you — expectations, a request, demand, or cheers. ファンの声援に応えて ('in response to the fans' cheers'). The noun is typically 期待・要望・要求・声援 — something the subject then satisfies.
pitfalls: It pairs with nouns of expectation or demand (期待・要望・要求・声援), not with just any noun.
応える here means 'to meet / live up to' (written 応), distinct from 答える 'to answer a question' — both read こたえる.

examples.ja: 消費者の要望に応えて、新しいサービスが始まった。
examples.en: In response to consumer demand, a new service was launched.
examples.f: ｜消費[しょうひ]｜者[しゃ]の｜要望[ようぼう]に｜応[こた]えて、｜新[あたら]しいサービスが｜始[はじ]まった。

examples.ja: 選手たちは、応援してくれた人々の期待に応えて優勝した。
examples.en: The players lived up to the expectations of those who cheered them on and won the championship.
examples.f: ｜選手[せんしゅ]たちは、｜応援[おうえん]してくれた｜人々[ひとびと]の｜期待[きたい]に｜応[こた]えて｜優勝[ゆうしょう]した。

related.note: に沿って means following a plan or wish without straying; に応えて means actively satisfying a demand aimed at you.
にしたがって means acting in obedience to an instruction; に応えて means fulfilling what others hope for from you.

title: に際して
meaning: on the occasion of; at the time of
summary: に際して marks a special or significant occasion at which something is done — 入学に際して ('on the occasion of enrolling'). It is formal and reserved for notable events such as ceremonies, departures, or beginnings, not everyday moments.
pitfalls: Reserved for weighty, often one-time occasions; for ordinary, repeated times use 〜時 instead.
Very formal (speeches, notices, documents); overusing it in casual talk sounds stiff.

examples.ja: 契約に際して、こちらの書類にご記入ください。
examples.en: At the time of signing the contract, please fill in these documents.
examples.f: ｜契約[けいやく]に｜際[さい]して、こちらの｜書類[しょるい]にご｜記入[きにゅう]ください。

examples.ja: 卒業に際して、お世話になった先生に感謝の言葉を述べた。
examples.en: On the occasion of graduating, I expressed words of gratitude to the teacher who had helped me.
examples.f: ｜卒業[そつぎょう]に｜際[さい]して、お｜世話[せわ]になった｜先生[せんせい]に｜感謝[かんしゃ]の｜言葉[ことば]を｜述[の]べた。

synonyms.note: にあたって is a near-synonym for a special occasion; に際して leans slightly more formal and written.

related.note: に先立ち marks acting in advance of an event; に際して marks acting at the moment of the event itself.

title: に先立ち
meaning: before; prior to; ahead of
summary: に先立ち／に先立って marks what comes before a significant event, often preparations made in advance — 開会に先立ち挨拶があった ('prior to the opening there was a greeting'). に先立ち is the slightly more formal, written stem form of に先立って.
structure: Noun ＋ に先立って／に先立ち
pitfalls: It stresses acting in advance of a notable event (often preparing for it); for a plain 'before doing X' in daily life, 前に is more natural.
The main event takes に; don't mark it with を.

examples.ja: 新製品の発売に先立ち、記者向けの説明会が開かれた。
examples.en: Prior to the release of the new product, a briefing for journalists was held.
examples.f: ｜新[しん]｜製品[せいひん]の｜発売[はつばい]に｜先立[さきだ]ち、｜記者[きしゃ]｜向[む]けの｜説明[せつめい]｜会[かい]が｜開[ひら]かれた。

examples.ja: 工事を始めるに先立って、近所の住民に説明会を開いた。
examples.en: Before starting construction, they held an information session for the local residents.
examples.f: ｜工事[こうじ]を｜始[はじ]めるに｜先立[さきだ]って、｜近所[きんじょ]の｜住民[じゅうみん]に｜説明[せつめい]｜会[かい]を｜開[ひら]いた。

synonyms.note: 前に is the everyday 'before'; に先立ち is formal and reserved for advance steps ahead of a major event.

related.note: に際して marks the moment of the event; に先立ち marks what is done ahead of it.

title: にしたら・にすれば
meaning: from the standpoint of; as far as ~ is concerned
summary: Noun＋にしたら／にすれば takes another person's standpoint and imagines how things look or feel to them — 親にしてみれば心配なのだろう ('from the parents' side, they must be worried'). The noun is almost always a person or group whose feelings are being pictured.
structure: Noun ＋ にしたら／にすれば／にしてみれば
pitfalls: Used with people or groups, and typically to speculate about their feelings — not for objective measurements or non-human standpoints.
Close to にとって, but にしたら／にすれば leans toward imagining someone's emotional reaction, while にとって states more neutrally what something means for them.

examples.ja: 冗談のつもりでも、言われた人にすれば深く傷つくこともある。
examples.en: Even if it's meant as a joke, from the standpoint of the person told, it can sometimes hurt deeply.
examples.f: ｜冗談[じょうだん]のつもりでも、｜言[い]われた｜人[ひと]にすれば｜深[ふか]く｜傷[きず]つくこともある。

examples.ja: 親にしたら、子供がいくつになっても心配なものだ。
examples.en: From a parent's point of view, no matter how old their child gets, they worry.
examples.f: ｜親[おや]にしたら、｜子供[こども]がいくつになっても｜心配[しんぱい]なものだ。

synonyms.note: にとって neutrally states what something means for someone; にしたら／にすれば colors it with their imagined feelings.
からすると／からすれば can judge from any basis or evidence; にしたら／にすれば adopts a person's own perspective.

title: にしても〜にしても
meaning: whether ~ or ~; regardless of which
summary: Pairing にしても…にしても lists two representative cases — often opposites — and says the same thing holds either way. 行くにしても行かないにしても早く決めてほしい ('whether you go or not, decide soon'). It covers both alternatives at once.
structure: Noun／Verb［plain form］＋ にしても ＋ Noun／Verb［plain form］＋ にしても
pitfalls: The two items are usually a matched pair — opposites, or two examples from the same set — not random unrelated nouns.
にしろ〜にしろ and にせよ〜にせよ mean the same; the しても form is the most neutral and common, the others more formal or emphatic.

examples.ja: 参加するにしても参加しないにしても、必ず返事をしてください。
examples.en: Whether you take part or not, please be sure to reply.
examples.f: ｜参加[さんか]するにしても｜参加[さんか]しないにしても、｜必[かなら]ず｜返事[へんじ]をしてください。

examples.ja: 電車にしてもバスにしても、この時間はとても混んでいる。
examples.en: Whether by train or by bus, at this hour it's very crowded.
examples.f: ｜電車[でんしゃ]にしてもバスにしても、この｜時間[じかん]はとても｜混[こ]んでいる。

synonyms.note: にしろ〜にしろ is the same 'whether A or B' in a firmer, more formal tone.
いずれにしても sums up 'either way' without re-listing the two cases; にしても〜にしても spells both out.

related.note: にしても alone means 'even if / even so'; doubled as にしても〜にしても it lists two cases that lead to the same result.

title: にしろ〜にしろ
meaning: whether ~ or ~
summary: にしろ…にしろ lists two cases and asserts the statement applies to both — やるにしろやめるにしろ自分で決めなさい ('whether you do it or quit, decide for yourself'). にしろ is a somewhat formal, firm variant of にしても…にしても.
structure: Noun／Verb［plain form］＋ にしろ ＋ Noun／Verb［plain form］＋ にしろ
pitfalls: The paired items are typically two opposites or two examples of one category, covering the range between them.
にしろ is the more formal counterpart of にしても; にせよ is its even more written-style equivalent — the meaning stays the same.

examples.ja: 賛成するにしろ反対するにしろ、理由をはっきり述べる必要がある。
examples.en: Whether you agree or disagree, you need to state your reasons clearly.
examples.f: ｜賛成[さんせい]するにしろ｜反対[はんたい]するにしろ、｜理由[りゆう]をはっきり｜述[の]べる｜必要[ひつよう]がある。

examples.ja: 大人にしろ子供にしろ、ルールは守らなければならない。
examples.en: Whether adult or child, the rules must be followed.
examples.f: ｜大人[おとな]にしろ｜子供[こども]にしろ、ルールは｜守[まも]らなければならない。

synonyms.note: にしても〜にしても is the same structure in a plainer, more neutral register.
にせよ〜にせよ is the most written-style version of the same 'whether A or B'.

related.note: いずれにしても concludes 'either way' in one phrase; にしろ〜にしろ names both cases explicitly.

title: に過ぎない
meaning: no more than; merely; just
summary: に過ぎない downplays something as being nothing more than what precedes it — ただの噂に過ぎない ('it's nothing but a rumor'). It minimizes the scale or importance of the thing, often to push back against an overestimation.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ に過ぎない
pitfalls: It belittles or limits ('only that, nothing beyond'), and often pairs with ただ／ほんの ('mere') for emphasis.
With nouns, attach directly with no だ: 言い訳に過ぎない, not 言い訳だに過ぎない.

examples.ja: これはほんの一例に過ぎず、ほかにも多くの問題がある。
examples.en: This is merely one example; there are many other problems as well.
examples.f: これはほんの｜一[いち]｜例[れい]に｜過[す]ぎず、ほかにも｜多[おお]くの｜問題[もんだい]がある。

examples.ja: 彼はただ命令に従ったに過ぎないと主張した。
examples.en: He insisted that he had merely followed orders.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はただ｜命令[めいれい]に｜従[したが]ったに｜過[す]ぎないと｜主張[しゅちょう]した。

synonyms.note: のみ is a formal 'only' limiting quantity; に過ぎない adds the judgment that it's unimportantly small.
だけ neutrally marks 'only'; に過ぎない spins that 'only' as a dismissive 'merely, nothing more'.

related.note: にほかならない emphatically insists something is precisely X; に過ぎない dismisses it as no more than X.

title: にせよ・にしろ
meaning: even if; granted that; whether ~ or ~
summary: にせよ (and its variant にしろ) concedes a case — 'even if; granted that' — then states something that holds regardless. どんな理由があるにせよ暴力は許されない ('whatever the reason, violence is not allowed'). にせよ is the formal, written form; paired as AにせよBにせよ it means 'whether A or B'.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ にせよ／にしろ
pitfalls: にせよ is formal and literary — common in writing and speeches, but stiff in casual chat, where にしても fits better.
It often follows a question word (どんな・誰・いつ) to mean 'no matter what / who / when'.

examples.ja: 冗談にせよ、人が傷つくようなことは言うべきではない。
examples.en: Even as a joke, you shouldn't say things that hurt people.
examples.f: ｜冗談[じょうだん]にせよ、｜人[ひと]が｜傷[きず]つくようなことは｜言[い]うべきではない。

examples.ja: 結果がどうであるにせよ、最後まで全力を尽くすつもりだ。
examples.en: Whatever the outcome may be, I intend to give it my all to the very end.
examples.f: ｜結果[けっか]がどうであるにせよ、｜最後[さいご]まで｜全力[ぜんりょく]を｜尽[つ]くすつもりだ。

synonyms.note: にしろ〜にしろ pairs two cases; にせよ is the same word and can stand alone as 'even if / granted that'.
としても is the everyday 'even if / even supposing'; にせよ is its more formal, written-style counterpart.

related.note: いずれにせよ concludes 'in any case, either way'; にせよ concedes a single case ('even if it's X').

title: に相違ない
meaning: without a doubt; there is no mistaking
summary: に相違ない expresses the speaker's firm, reasoned conviction that something must be true — 'without a doubt; there's no mistaking it'. It is the formal, written-style counterpart of に違いない, common in essays, legal, and literary contexts.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ に相違ない
pitfalls: Formal and written; in everyday speech に違いない (or casual に決まっている) is far more natural.
Attach directly to the plain form; no だ after a noun or な-adjective: 犯人に相違ない, not 犯人だに相違ない.

examples.ja: これだけの証拠がある以上、彼が犯人に相違ない。
examples.en: Given this much evidence, he is without a doubt the culprit.
examples.f: これだけの｜証拠[しょうこ]がある｜以上[いじょう]、｜彼[かれ]が｜犯人[はんにん]に｜相違[そうい]ない。

examples.ja: あの慌てた様子から見て、何か問題が起きたに相違ない。
examples.en: Judging from that flustered manner, something must certainly have gone wrong.
examples.f: あの｜慌[あわ]てた｜様子[ようす]から｜見[み]て、｜何[なに]か｜問題[もんだい]が｜起[お]きたに｜相違[そうい]ない。

synonyms.note: に違いない is the ordinary 'must be, no doubt'; に相違ない is its formal, written-register twin.
に決まっている is a casual, emotional 'obviously'; に相違ない is a formal, reasoned 'without a doubt'.

related.note: はずだ is a logical expectation open to revision; に相違ない asserts near-certainty with no room for doubt.

title: に沿って
meaning: along; in accordance with
summary: に沿って has two linked senses: physically 'along' something long (川に沿って歩く = 'walk along the river') and figuratively 'in line with' a plan, rule, or wish (計画に沿って進める = 'proceed in accordance with the plan'). The core image is following the length or intent of something without departing from it.
structure: Noun ＋ に沿って／に沿った
pitfalls: It covers both a physical line (道路に沿って) and an abstract guideline (方針に沿って); context tells them apart.
The attributive form before a noun is に沿った: ご要望に沿った提案 ('a proposal in line with your wishes').

examples.ja: この道に沿ってまっすぐ行くと、右手に駅が見えます。
examples.en: If you go straight along this road, you'll see the station on your right.
examples.f: この｜道[みち]に｜沿[そ]ってまっすぐ｜行[い]くと、｜右手[みぎて]に｜駅[えき]が｜見[み]えます。

examples.ja: お客様のご希望に沿って、旅行の計画を立てました。
examples.en: In accordance with the customer's wishes, we drew up the travel plan.
examples.f: お｜客様[きゃくさま]のご｜希望[きぼう]に｜沿[そ]って、｜旅行[りょこう]の｜計画[けいかく]を｜立[た]てました。

synonyms.note: にしたがって means acting in obedience to a rule or instruction; に沿って means keeping in line with a plan, path, or wish.
に基づいて means grounding an action on a basis or source; に沿って means staying aligned with a guideline or intent.

related.note: に応えて means actively fulfilling a demand aimed at you; に沿って means proceeding in line with a plan or wish.

title: につき
meaning: due to; per; each
summary: につき has two main uses. As 'due to', it gives a reason in formal notices — 本日は定休日につき休業します ('as today is a regular holiday, we are closed'). As 'per', it states a rate — 一つにつき百円 ('100 yen each'). Both are set, somewhat formal uses of the same につき.
pitfalls: The 'due to' sense is formal and written — typical of signs and announcements, not casual speech (use から／ので there).
Tell the two senses apart by context: reason (定休日につき) versus rate (ひとりにつき).

examples.ja: 準備中につき、しばらくお待ちください。
examples.en: As we are still preparing, please wait a while.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]｜中[ちゅう]につき、しばらくお｜待[ま]ちください。

examples.ja: この商品は、おひとりにつき三つまで購入できます。
examples.en: You may buy up to three of this item per person.
examples.f: この｜商品[しょうひん]は、おひとりにつき｜三[みっ]つまで｜購入[こうにゅう]できます。

synonyms.note: 当たり covers the 'per unit' rate sense; につき shares that sense but also means 'due to', which 当たり never does.

related.note: ために gives a reason in ordinary registers; につき in its 'due to' sense is the stiffer, notice-style equivalent.

title: につけ
meaning: every time; whenever
summary: につけ means 'every time / whenever' a certain thing happens, some feeling or thought naturally arises — この写真を見るにつけ昔を思い出す ('whenever I look at this photo, I recall the old days'). It is literary, usually followed by a spontaneous emotion or reflection, and often appears doubled (何かにつけ, 良きにつけ悪しきにつけ).
pitfalls: It typically leads to an involuntary feeling or memory (思い出す・感じる), not a deliberate action.
Literary and somewhat fixed; for a plain 'every time' in everyday speech, たびに is more natural.

examples.ja: この曲を聞くにつけ、学生時代を思い出す。
examples.en: Whenever I hear this song, I remember my student days.
examples.f: この｜曲[きょく]を｜聞[き]くにつけ、｜学生[がくせい]｜時代[じだい]を｜思い出[おもいだ]す。

examples.ja: ニュースを見るにつけ、平和のありがたさを感じる。
examples.en: Every time I watch the news, I feel grateful for peace.
examples.f: ニュースを｜見[み]るにつけ、｜平和[へいわ]のありがたさを｜感[かん]じる。

synonyms.note: たびに is the everyday 'every time' for any repeated action; につけ is literary and leads to a spontaneous feeling.

title: にて
meaning: in; at; by; with (formal, written で)
summary: にて is the formal, written-language counterpart of the particle で. It marks the place where something happens (会場にて), the means or method used (メールにて), or the time and circumstances — exactly like で, but in a stiffer register found in notices, invitations, business letters, and ceremonies. In ordinary conversation, で is used instead.
pitfalls: にて belongs to formal, written contexts (announcements, ceremonies, business correspondence); in everyday speech で is normal, not にて.
It stands in only for the particle で; it does not replace the で that is the て-form of the copula だ (as in 学生で、〜).

examples.ja: 本日の説明会は、三階の会議室にて開催いたします。
examples.en: Today's briefing session will be held in the conference room on the third floor.
examples.f: ｜本日[ほんじつ]の｜説明[せつめい]｜会[かい]は、｜三[さん]｜階[かい]の｜会議[かいぎ]｜室[しつ]にて｜開催[かいさい]いたします。

examples.ja: 詳しい結果につきましては、後日メールにてお知らせいたします。
examples.en: As for the detailed results, we will inform you later by email.
examples.f: ｜詳[くわ]しい｜結果[けっか]につきましては、｜後日[ごじつ]メールにてお｜知[し]らせいたします。

synonyms.note: で is the everyday particle for place and means; にて is its formal, written-language equivalent.

related.note: において also marks a formal place or situation and is even stiffer; にて is closer to a direct swap for で.

title: に伴って・に伴い
kana: にともなって・にともない
meaning: along with; as; accompanying (a change)
summary: に伴って (and its stiffer form に伴い) links two changes: as the first situation develops or changes, a second one follows along with it as a natural accompaniment or consequence — 人口の増加に伴って = along with the rise in population. It attaches to a noun, or to a dictionary-form verb + の. The register is formal, common in news and reports.
pitfalls: Both sides normally describe a change or development, one accompanying the other; it is not used to join two static, unrelated facts.
に伴い is the more formal, written form of に伴って; the meaning is the same.

examples.ja: 経済の発展に伴って、人々の暮らしも大きく変わってきた。
examples.en: Along with economic development, people's lives have changed greatly as well.
examples.f: ｜経済[けいざい]の｜発展[はってん]に｜伴[ともな]って、｜人々[ひとびと]の｜暮[く]らしも｜大[おお]きく｜変[か]わってきた。

examples.ja: 台風の接近に伴い、多くの電車が運転を見合わせている。
examples.en: With the approach of the typhoon, many trains are suspending their service.
examples.f: ｜台風[たいふう]の｜接近[せっきん]に｜伴[ともな]い、｜多[おお]くの｜電車[でんしゃ]が｜運転[うんてん]を｜見合[みあ]わせている。

synonyms.note: につれて also links two gradual, proportional changes; に伴って also covers one-off consequences that accompany an event.
にしたがって likewise expresses one change tracking another; the two overlap closely in this 'as ~ changes' sense.

related.note: と共に can mean 'as ~ changes' too; に伴って foregrounds one change accompanying or causing another.

title: にほかならない
meaning: is nothing but; is none other than
summary: にほかならない attaches to a noun to declare emphatically that something is 'nothing other than' that noun — the speaker rules out every other explanation and insists this is the true identity or cause. 成功は努力の結果にほかならない = success is nothing but the fruit of effort. The tone is assertive and written.
pitfalls: It pins down a single, definitive identity or cause, and is far more insistent than a plain だ or である.
It attaches to nouns, including clauses nominalized with の／こと; it does not attach directly to a plain verb or adjective.

examples.ja: 今回の勝利は、チーム全員の努力の結果にほかならない。
examples.en: This victory is nothing other than the result of the whole team's effort.
examples.f: ｜今回[こんかい]の｜勝利[しょうり]は、チーム｜全員[ぜんいん]の｜努力[どりょく]の｜結果[けっか]にほかならない。

examples.ja: この決定は、住民の声を無視したものにほかならない。
examples.en: This decision is nothing but a disregard for the residents' voices.
examples.f: この｜決定[けってい]は、｜住民[じゅうみん]の｜声[こえ]を｜無視[むし]したものにほかならない。

related.note: に過ぎない shares the frame but downplays — 'no more than'; にほかならない elevates — 'precisely this and nothing else'.
こそ also singles something out emphatically as 'precisely'; にほかならない specifically equates a fact with its one true cause.

title: に向かって・に向けて
kana: にむかって・にむけて
meaning: toward; heading for; aimed at
summary: に向かって and に向けて both mark a target that one moves or acts toward. に向かって is more physical and directional — facing or heading toward a place or person (海に向かって叫ぶ). に向けて leans toward a goal or aim — preparing or working toward a target, event, deadline, or audience (試験に向けて勉強する).
structure: Noun ＋ に向かって／に向けて
pitfalls: に向かって tends to be literal direction or facing (北に向かって歩く); に向けて tends to be a goal aimed at (大会に向けて). They overlap but are not always interchangeable.
Distinguish this from に向いている ('to be suited to'), which is a different expression built on the same verb.

examples.ja: 子供たちは大きな声で、海に向かって自分の名前を呼んだ。
examples.en: The children called out their own names loudly toward the sea.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]たちは｜大[おお]きな｜声[こえ]で、｜海[うみ]に｜向[む]かって｜自分[じぶん]の｜名前[なまえ]を｜呼[よ]んだ。

examples.ja: 来年の大会に向けて、選手たちは厳しい練習を続けている。
examples.en: Heading toward next year's tournament, the athletes keep up their tough training.
examples.f: ｜来年[らいねん]の｜大会[たいかい]に｜向[む]けて、｜選手[せんしゅ]たちは｜厳[きび]しい｜練習[れんしゅう]を｜続[つづ]けている。

related.note: に対して marks the target of an action or attitude ('toward / against'); に向かって・に向けて marks physical direction or a goal aimed at.

title: にもかかわらず
meaning: despite; even though; nevertheless
summary: にもかかわらず means 'despite / even though' — the second clause happens contrary to what the first would lead you to expect. 雨にもかかわらず = despite the rain; 努力したにもかかわらず = even though (someone) tried hard. It attaches to nouns and to plain-form clauses, and carries a formal tone, often of surprise or dissatisfaction at the unexpected outcome.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ にもかかわらず
pitfalls: Do not confuse it with にかかわらず ('regardless of, whether or not'), which sets aside a range of options; にもかかわらず points to one fact that the result contradicts.
It is more formal than のに, and often colored with surprise or complaint at the unexpected result.

examples.ja: 十分に準備したにもかかわらず、試験の結果は思わしくなかった。
examples.en: Despite having prepared thoroughly, the exam results were not what I had hoped for.
examples.f: ｜十分[じゅうぶん]に｜準備[じゅんび]したにもかかわらず、｜試験[しけん]の｜結果[けっか]は｜思[おも]わしくなかった。

examples.ja: 悪天候にもかかわらず、多くの人が会場に集まった。
examples.en: In spite of the bad weather, many people gathered at the venue.
examples.f: ｜悪天候[あくてんこう]にもかかわらず、｜多[おお]くの｜人[ひと]が｜会場[かいじょう]に｜集[あつ]まった。

synonyms.note: のに also marks an unexpected, contrary result; にもかかわらず is more formal and written.
ものの also concedes 'although'; にもかかわらず stresses a result defying a clear expectation.

related.note: ながらも 'although' attaches to a stem or adjective and is more compact; にもかかわらず works after full clauses and nouns.

title: にわたって
meaning: throughout; over; spanning (a period or range)
summary: にわたって marks that something extends across the whole of a span — a period, an area, or a range of items. 三日間にわたって = over (the full) three days; 全国にわたって = across the entire country. The noun before it names the scope. Before a noun, the form becomes にわたる (長期にわたる交渉). The register is formal and written.
pitfalls: The preceding noun states the extent covered (time, distance, area, or number), so it needs breadth, not a single point in time.
Before a noun, use にわたる (長期にわたる交渉), not にわたって.

examples.ja: 会議は数時間にわたって続き、参加者はみな疲れ切っていた。
examples.en: The meeting went on for hours on end, and all the participants were worn out.
examples.f: ｜会議[かいぎ]は｜数[すう]｜時間[じかん]にわたって｜続[つづ]き、｜参加[さんか]｜者[しゃ]はみな｜疲[つか]れ｜切[き]っていた。

examples.ja: この作家の作品は、幅広い世代にわたって読まれている。
examples.en: This author's works are read across a wide range of generations.
examples.f: この｜作家[さっか]の｜作品[さくひん]は、｜幅広[はばひろ]い｜世代[せだい]にわたって｜読[よ]まれている。

synonyms.note: を通じて・を通して also means 'throughout / across'; にわたって stresses the full breadth of the span, を通じて the continuity through it.
にかけて 'over / through' runs from one point to another; にわたって covers the entire extent of a range.

title: 〜ぬ
meaning: not (classical negative, = ない)
summary: 〜ぬ is the classical negative ending, equivalent to modern 〜ない. It attaches to the same stem as ない (知らぬ = 知らない, 思わぬ = 思わない), with the irregular せぬ for する and 来ぬ(こぬ) for 来る. Today it survives mainly in set phrases, proverbs, and a stiff literary or archaic tone (見知らぬ人, 思わぬ結果).
structure: する → せぬ ／ 来る → 来ぬ（こぬ）
pitfalls: It attaches to the same stem as ない (行かぬ, 知らぬ), and する becomes せぬ, not しぬ.
The colloquial 知らん is a contraction of this 知らぬ／知らない; sentence-final ぬ itself sounds literary or fixed, not everyday speech.
Before a noun it works attributively (見知らぬ土地 = an unfamiliar place).

examples.ja: 世の中には、知らぬほうが幸せなこともある。
examples.en: In this world, there are things you are happier not knowing.
examples.f: ｜世の中[よのなか]には、｜知[し]らぬほうが｜幸[しあわ]せなこともある。

examples.ja: 彼は困っている人を見て、見ぬふりはできなかった。
examples.en: Seeing someone in trouble, he could not just pretend not to notice.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜困[こま]っている｜人[ひと]を｜見[み]て、｜見[み]ぬふりはできなかった。

synonyms.note: 〜ざる is the classical negative used attributively before a noun; ぬ is its plain sentence-ending counterpart, overlapping closely.

related.note: ずに 'without doing' comes from the same classical negative ず; ぬ is the counterpart meaning simply 'not'.

title: 抜きで・抜きにして
meaning: without; leaving out; setting aside
summary: 〜抜きで and 〜抜きにして mean doing something while leaving out a normally-expected element. 朝食抜きで = without breakfast; 冗談抜きで = joking aside. 〜は抜きにして ('let's leave ~ out') often opens a suggestion to set something aside. It attaches to a noun. The related 〜を抜きにしては + negative means the following would be impossible without it.
structure: Noun ＋ 抜きで／抜きにして
Noun ＋ を抜きにしては ＋ ～ない
pitfalls: It attaches to a noun; to say 'without doing (a verb)', use ないで or ずに, not 抜き.
〜を抜きにしては／抜きには + a negative means the following is impossible without it (彼の協力を抜きにしては成功しなかった).

examples.ja: 今日は堅い話は抜きにして、みんなで楽しく飲みましょう。
examples.en: Let's leave the stiff talk aside today and just enjoy some drinks together.
examples.f: ｜今日[きょう]は｜堅[かた]い｜話[はなし]は｜抜[ぬ]きにして、みんなで｜楽[たの]しく｜飲[の]みましょう。

examples.ja: 地元の人々の協力を抜きにして、この祭りは成り立たない。
examples.en: Without the cooperation of the local people, this festival could not be held.
examples.f: ｜地元[じもと]の｜人々[ひとびと]の｜協力[きょうりょく]を｜抜[ぬ]きにして、この｜祭[まつ]りは｜成り立[なりた]たない。

synonyms.note: 〜なし simply states a noun's absence ('without ~'); 抜き stresses deliberately leaving out something normally included.
なしに・なしで also means 'without'; 抜きにして often carries the nuance 'let's set aside / omit on purpose'.

title: 〜抜く
meaning: to do all the way through; to see through to the end (despite hardship)
summary: 〜抜く attaches to the ます-stem and says an action was carried all the way to the end, usually against difficulty — 走り抜く = run all the way through, 考え抜く = think something through completely, やり抜く = see it through to the finish. The nuance is persistence and endurance, not mere completion. It conjugates as an う-verb (抜いた, 抜いて).
pitfalls: Attach it to the stem: やり抜く, not やる抜く.
〜抜く stresses enduring through hardship to the finish, while 〜切る stresses using something up or reaching a clean end — 戦い抜く (fight all the way through) vs 使い切る (use it all up).

examples.ja: どんなに苦しくても、最後まで走り抜くつもりだ。
examples.en: No matter how hard it gets, I intend to run all the way to the finish.
examples.f: どんなに｜苦[くる]しくても、｜最後[さいご]まで｜走り抜[はしりぬ]くつもりだ。

examples.ja: 悩み抜いた末に、彼女は会社を辞める決心をした。
examples.en: After agonizing over it thoroughly, she made up her mind to quit the company.
examples.f: ｜悩み抜[なやみぬ]いた｜末[すえ]に、｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜会社[かいしゃ]を｜辞[や]める｜決心[けっしん]をした。

synonyms.note: 〜切る also means 'do thoroughly / completely'; 抜く emphasizes persevering through hardship, 切る emphasizes finishing off entirely.
〜通す means 'keep doing all the way through'; 抜く adds the sense of pushing through difficulty to the end.

related.note: 〜終わる neutrally marks finishing an action; 抜く adds the effort and endurance of reaching the end.

title: ねばならない
meaning: must; have to (formal, literary)
summary: 〜ねばならない is a formal, somewhat literary way to say 'must / have to.' It attaches to the same stem as ない, plus ねばならない (行かねばならない = 行かなければならない), with せねばならない for する. It is the stiff, written counterpart of なければならない, common in editorials, speeches, and formal prose. It can shorten to ねばならぬ or just ねば.
structure: Verb［ない-stem］＋ ねばならない
する → せねばならない
pitfalls: It attaches to the ない-stem (守らねばならない), and する becomes せねばならない, not しねばならない.
The register is formal and written; in everyday speech なければならない or なきゃ is used instead.

examples.ja: 我々は、この問題に真剣に取り組まねばならない。
examples.en: We must tackle this problem in earnest.
examples.f: ｜我々[われわれ]は、この｜問題[もんだい]に｜真剣[しんけん]に｜取り組[とりく]まねばならない。

examples.ja: 約束した以上、必ず果たさねばならないと彼は考えていた。
examples.en: He felt that, having made the promise, he absolutely had to follow through.
examples.f: ｜約束[やくそく]した｜以上[いじょう]、｜必[かなら]ず｜果[は]たさねばならないと｜彼[かれ]は｜考[かんが]えていた。

synonyms.note: なければならない is the everyday 'must'; ねばならない is its formal, written equivalent.
なくてはならない also means 'must'; ねばならない is stiffer and more literary.

related.note: ざるを得ない means 'have no choice but to'; ねばならない states an obligation rather than reluctant inevitability.

title: の上では
meaning: as far as ~ goes; on paper; in terms of
summary: 〜の上では means 'as far as ~ goes / on the level of ~' — judging by a document, calculation, or nominal standard, often implying that reality may differ. 計算の上では = by calculation (in theory); 法律の上では = legally speaking (on paper). It frequently sets up a contrast with how things actually are.
pitfalls: Here 上 is read うえ and means 'on the level / basis of', not a physical 'on top of'.
It often implies the real situation differs from the stated standard (数字の上では回復したが、実感はない).

examples.ja: カレンダーの上ではもう春だが、まだ雪が残っている地域も多い。
examples.en: On the calendar it is already spring, yet in many areas snow still remains.
examples.f: カレンダーの｜上[うえ]ではもう｜春[はる]だが、まだ｜雪[ゆき]が｜残[のこ]っている｜地域[ちいき]も｜多[おお]い。

examples.ja: 契約の上では問題ないが、実際の運用にはまだ課題が残っている。
examples.en: On paper the contract is fine, but there are still issues with how it works in practice.
examples.f: ｜契約[けいやく]の｜上[うえ]では｜問題[もんだい]ないが、｜実際[じっさい]の｜運用[うんよう]にはまだ｜課題[かだい]が｜残[のこ]っている。

related.note: 〜上で means 'upon doing / in the process of' — a different use of 上; の上では means 'on the nominal level of ~, as opposed to reality'.

title: のうち(で)
meaning: among; out of; of the (group)
summary: 〜のうち(で) marks the group or range from which something is singled out — 'among / out of.' 四人のうちで一番背が高い = the tallest of the four; 一年のうちで = within (the span of) a year. It commonly appears with superlatives or when picking a subset out of a whole, and is close to 〜の中で.
pitfalls: With comparisons it names the set being compared (three of us, this list); it overlaps closely with 〜の中で.
うちに (with に) means 'while / before' a state ends — a different meaning from うち(で) 'among'.

examples.ja: クラスの学生のうちで、彼女が最も熱心に勉強している。
examples.en: Among the students in the class, she studies the most eagerly.
examples.f: クラスの｜学生[がくせい]のうちで、｜彼女[かのじょ]が｜最[もっと]も｜熱心[ねっしん]に｜勉強[べんきょう]している。

examples.ja: 一年のうちで、この時期が一番過ごしやすい。
examples.en: Of the whole year, this season is the most comfortable to get through.
examples.f: ｜一[いち]｜年[ねん]のうちで、この｜時期[じき]が｜一番[いちばん]｜過[す]ごしやすい。

related.note: うちに means 'while / before (a state ends)'; のうちで picks one out of a group.

title: のではないだろうか
meaning: isn't it (perhaps) that ~?; I rather think that ~
summary: 〜のではないだろうか is a soft, tentative way to put forward an opinion — literally 'isn't it perhaps that ~?', i.e. 'I rather think that ~.' It hedges a claim so it sounds considered rather than blunt: 彼は無理をしているのではないだろうか = I wonder if he isn't overdoing it. Common in essays and careful speech. のではないでしょうか is the polite form.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ のではないだろうか
な-adjective／Noun ＋ なの ＋ ではないだろうか
pitfalls: It softens the speaker's own opinion; it is not a real question expecting an answer.
The contractions んじゃないだろうか／んじゃないか are more casual; のではないでしょうか is the polite version.

examples.ja: このままでは、環境への影響がさらに深刻になるのではないだろうか。
examples.en: At this rate, won't the impact on the environment become even more serious, I wonder.
examples.f: このままでは、｜環境[かんきょう]への｜影響[えいきょう]がさらに｜深刻[しんこく]になるのではないだろうか。

examples.ja: 彼の説明には、どこか無理があるのではないだろうか。
examples.en: I can't help thinking there is something forced in his explanation.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜説明[せつめい]には、どこか｜無理[むり]があるのではないだろうか。

related.note: ではないか asserts or seeks agreement more directly; のではないだろうか is softer, voicing one's own tentative guess.
だろう states a plain conjecture 'probably'; のではないだろうか wraps that guess in a gentle rhetorical question.

title: のみ
meaning: only; just; nothing but (formal)
summary: のみ is the formal, written-language equivalent of だけ, meaning 'only / just.' 会員のみ = members only; 見守るのみだ = do nothing but watch over. It appears in notices, contracts, and formal prose, while conversation uses だけ. It attaches to nouns and to plain-form verbs.
pitfalls: のみ belongs to formal, written style; everyday speech uses だけ.
Do not confuse standalone のみ ('only') with のみならず ('not only ~ but also'), a separate expression.

examples.ja: 当店の駐車場は、ご予約のお客様のみご利用いただけます。
examples.en: Our parking lot may be used only by customers who have made a reservation.
examples.f: ｜当店[とうてん]の｜駐車[ちゅうしゃ]｜場[じょう]は、ご｜予約[よやく]のお｜客様[きゃくさま]のみご｜利用[りよう]いただけます。

examples.ja: 今はただ、彼の無事を祈るのみだ。
examples.en: For now, all I can do is pray for his safety.
examples.f: ｜今[いま]はただ、｜彼[かれ]の｜無事[ぶじ]を｜祈[いの]るのみだ。

synonyms.note: だけ is the everyday 'only'; のみ is its formal, written equivalent.
しか〜ない 'only, nothing but' requires a negative verb; のみ is affirmative and formal.

related.note: のみならず ('not only ~ but also') is built on this のみ.

title: のみならず
meaning: not only ~ but also
summary: のみならず means 'not only ~ but also,' the formal counterpart of だけでなく. It states one fact and then adds a further, often broader one: 国内のみならず海外でも = not only domestically but abroad as well. It attaches to nouns and plain-form clauses, and the second part is frequently marked with も. The register is formal and written.
pitfalls: It is formal and written; conversationally だけでなく is the natural choice.
The added element is usually equal to or larger in scope than the first, often marked with も.

examples.ja: この小説は国内のみならず、海外でも高く評価されている。
examples.en: This novel is highly regarded not only within Japan but abroad as well.
examples.f: この｜小説[しょうせつ]は｜国内[こくない]のみならず、｜海外[かいがい]でも｜高[たか]く｜評価[ひょうか]されている。

examples.ja: 彼は知識が豊富であるのみならず、それを分かりやすく伝える力もある。
examples.en: He is not only rich in knowledge but also has the ability to convey it clearly.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜知識[ちしき]が｜豊富[ほうふ]であるのみならず、それを｜分[わ]かりやすく｜伝[つた]える｜力[ちから]もある。

synonyms.note: だけでなく is the everyday 'not only ~ but also'; のみならず is its formal equivalent.
ばかりか 'not only ~ but even' highlights an escalating, often surprising addition; のみならず is more neutral and formal.
にとどまらず 'not stopping at ~' stresses going beyond a limit; のみならず simply adds a further element.

related.note: はもちろん 'not to mention' treats the first item as obvious; のみならず adds a further point in formal prose.

title: のも当然だ
meaning: it's only natural that ~; no wonder ~
summary: 〜のも当然だ means 'it's only natural that ~ / no wonder ~' — given the circumstances, the result or reaction is entirely to be expected. あれだけ練習したのだから、勝つのも当然だ = having practiced that much, of course they'd win. It attaches to a plain-form clause + のも, or to a noun + も.
pitfalls: 当然 is read とうぜん; the phrase judges a result to be the natural, expected consequence of a stated cause.
It is very close to のももっともだ; 当然だ leans more on 'obviously so', もっともだ on 'reasonable / understandable'.

examples.ja: あれだけひどいことを言われたのだから、彼女が怒るのも当然だ。
examples.en: Having been told something that awful, it's only natural that she got angry.
examples.f: あれだけひどいことを｜言[い]われたのだから、｜彼女[かのじょ]が｜怒[おこ]るのも｜当然[とうぜん]だ。

examples.ja: 準備を全くしていなかったのだから、失敗するのも当然だった。
examples.en: Since he hadn't prepared at all, it was no wonder he failed.
examples.f: ｜準備[じゅんび]を｜全[まった]くしていなかったのだから、｜失敗[しっぱい]するのも｜当然[とうぜん]だった。

synonyms.note: のももっともだ 'it's understandable that'; のも当然だ stresses that the result is the obvious, expected one.

related.note: わけだ 'that's why, no wonder'; のも当然だ explicitly labels the outcome as natural or deserved.
はずだ 'should be, expected'; のも当然だ judges a fact as a natural consequence rather than a logical expectation.

title: の下で
meaning: under; under the supervision / influence of
summary: 〜の下で(もとで) means acting 'under' someone or something — under their guidance, authority, or a set of conditions. 有名な先生の下で学ぶ = study under a famous teacher; 厳しい規則の下で = under strict rules. Here 下 is read もと and means a governing influence or circumstance, not a physical 'below'. の下に is a close variant.
pitfalls: 下 here is read もと (not した); it means 'under the influence / authority / conditions of', not physically underneath.
の下で often stresses the activity carried on under that condition; の下に can stress the resulting state or arrangement.

examples.ja: 彼は有名な研究者の下で、長年研究を続けてきた。
examples.en: He has continued his research for many years under a famous scholar.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜有名[ゆうめい]な｜研究[けんきゅう]｜者[しゃ]の｜下[もと]で、｜長年[ながねん]｜研究[けんきゅう]を｜続[つづ]けてきた。

examples.ja: 厳しい規則の下で、選手たちは日々練習に励んでいる。
examples.en: Under strict rules, the athletes devote themselves to practice day after day.
examples.f: ｜厳[きび]しい｜規則[きそく]の｜下[もと]で、｜選手[せんしゅ]たちは｜日々[ひび]｜練習[れんしゅう]に｜励[はげ]んでいる。

related.note: において marks a formal place or situation ('in / at'); の下で marks acting under a person's authority or a condition.
をもとに uses もと for a basis or source ('based on ~'); の下で means 'under the authority / conditions of'.

title: のももっともだ
meaning: it's understandable that ~; no wonder ~
summary: 〜のももっともだ means 'it's understandable / reasonable that ~' — given the situation, one can well see why someone feels or acts a certain way. ここまで待たされたら、彼が怒るのももっともだ = if he was kept waiting this long, it's understandable he got angry. もっとも here means 'reasonable, justified'. It attaches to a plain-form clause + のも.
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ のももっともだ
pitfalls: もっとも here means 'reasonable / justified' (もっともだ), not the adverb 最も 'most'.
It is very close to のも当然だ; もっともだ emphasizes that a reaction is understandable, 当然だ that a result is the obviously expected one.

examples.ja: あんな失礼な態度を取られたら、彼女が腹を立てるのももっともだ。
examples.en: If she was treated so rudely, it's quite understandable that she'd be upset.
examples.f: あんな｜失礼[しつれい]な｜態度[たいど]を｜取[と]られたら、｜彼女[かのじょ]が｜腹[はら]を｜立[た]てるのももっともだ。

examples.ja: これほど値上がりしては、客が減るのももっともだろう。
examples.en: With prices rising this much, it's only to be expected that customers would fall off.
examples.f: これほど｜値上[ねあ]がりしては、｜客[きゃく]が｜減[へ]るのももっともだろう。

synonyms.note: のも当然だ 'it's only natural'; のももっともだ stresses that a reaction is reasonable and understandable.

related.note: わけだ 'no wonder, that explains it'; のももっともだ specifically judges a reaction to be justified.

title: ばかりか
meaning: not only ~ but even ~
summary: 〜ばかりか means 'not only ~ but even ~' — it states one thing and then adds a second, usually more extreme or surprising, that goes beyond it. 手伝ってくれないばかりか、邪魔までした = not only did he not help, he even got in the way. The added part often takes も or さえ. It attaches to nouns and plain-form clauses.
pitfalls: The second element usually escalates beyond the first (often with も／さえ); it is not for adding a merely equal, neutral point.
The added fact is frequently unexpected or worse, so ばかりか often carries an emotional or evaluative colouring.

examples.ja: 彼は約束を破ったばかりか、謝ろうともしなかった。
examples.en: Not only did he break his promise, he didn't even try to apologize.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜約束[やくそく]を｜破[やぶ]ったばかりか、｜謝[あやま]ろうともしなかった。

examples.ja: その店は値段が安いばかりか、味も素晴らしいと評判だ。
examples.en: That restaurant has a reputation for being not only cheap but delicious on top of it.
examples.f: その｜店[みせ]は｜値段[ねだん]が｜安[やす]いばかりか、｜味[あじ]も｜素晴[すば]らしいと｜評判[ひょうばん]だ。

synonyms.note: だけでなく 'not only ~ but also' is neutral; ばかりか adds a stronger, often surprising second point.
のみならず is the formal 'not only ~ but also'; ばかりか highlights an escalating, often unexpected addition.
どころか 'far from ~, on the contrary'; ばかりか adds to the first fact, while どころか overturns it.

related.note: さえ 'even'; ばかりか frequently pairs with も／さえ in the added clause to mark the extra element.

title: 果たして
meaning: sure enough; just as expected; really ~? (intensifying doubt in a question)
summary: 果たして is an adverb with two related uses. Before a statement it means 'sure enough / just as one expected', confirming that a prediction came true. In a question — typically with か or のだろうか — it sharpens the doubt, 'really…? / I wonder if it truly…'. It belongs to careful, somewhat written or formal speech.
structure: 果たして ＋ Sentence［statement: 'as expected' sense］
果たして ＋ Sentence［question with か／のだろうか: 'really ~?' sense］
pitfalls: Two senses: before a plain statement it confirms an expectation ('sure enough'); before a question it deepens doubt ('really…?'). The question form tells them apart.
It leans formal and written; in casual speech やっぱり covers the 'as expected' meaning.

examples.ja: 果たして彼の予想どおり、試合は延期になった。
examples.en: Sure enough, just as he had predicted, the match was postponed.
examples.f: ｜果[は]たして｜彼[かれ]の｜予想[よそう]どおり、｜試合[しあい]は｜延期[えんき]になった。

examples.ja: 果たしてこの計画は本当に成功するのだろうか。
examples.en: Will this plan really succeed, I wonder?
examples.f: ｜果[は]たしてこの｜計画[けいかく]は｜本当[ほんとう]に｜成功[せいこう]するのだろうか。

related.note: 果たして…のだろうか pairs だろう with 'really?' emphasis; だろう alone is plain conjecture without that pointed doubt.

title: 〜ばと思います
meaning: I hope that ~; I would appreciate it if ~ (soft, humble wish)
summary: A conditional clause ending in ば followed by と思います voices a soft, humble hope — literally 'I think it would be good if…'. The いい ('would be good') after ば is usually left out, so 〜ばと思います on its own reads as a polite 'I hope / I'd be grateful if'. It is common in requests, notices, and speeches.
structure: Verb［ば form］＋ と思います
Verb［ば form］＋ （いい）＋ と思います
pitfalls: The いい ('it would be good') is normally dropped: 参加していただければと思います already means 'I hope you'll take part', with the wish left implicit.
It softens a request, so it is gentler and more humble than 〜てほしい or a plain imperative.

examples.ja: 皆様にもぜひご参加いただければと思います。
examples.en: I would be grateful if all of you would take part as well.
examples.f: ｜皆様[みなさま]にもぜひご｜参加[さんか]いただければと｜思[おも]います。

examples.ja: この資料が少しでも皆様のお役に立てばと思います。
examples.en: I hope this material will be of even a little help to you all.
examples.f: この｜資料[しりょう]が｜少[すこ]しでも｜皆様[みなさま]のお｜役に立[やくにた]てばと｜思[おも]います。

synonyms.note: ばいい plainly states 'it'd be good if'; 〜ばと思います wraps that in 思う for a humbler, more indirect wish.

related.note: てほしい directly says 'I want you to …'; 〜ばと思います is softer and more deferential.
the と思う here is the ordinary 'I think', which turns a conditional into a modest hope.

title: はともかく
meaning: setting ~ aside; regardless of ~; never mind ~, the point is
summary: 〜はともかく sets a topic aside as not the point right now, shifting the focus to what follows — 'never mind X, the real issue is Y'. Often 〜はともかく(として). X is downplayed as secondary here, not dismissed as unimportant in general.
structure: Noun ＋ はともかく（として）
Sentence ＋ か ＋ はともかく（として）
pitfalls: It parks X as 'not what matters now' and moves to a more important Y; it doesn't claim X is worthless overall, only that we're leaving it aside here.
After a question-like clause it takes か: 行くかどうかはともかく ('setting aside whether to go').

examples.ja: 味はともかく、この店は値段が安くて助かる。
examples.en: Taste aside, this shop is cheap, which is a real help.
examples.f: ｜味[あじ]はともかく、この｜店[みせ]は｜値段[ねだん]が｜安[やす]くて｜助[たす]かる。

examples.ja: 結果はともかく、最後まで全力を尽くしたことに意味がある。
examples.en: Regardless of the outcome, there is meaning in having given it my all to the end.
examples.f: ｜結果[けっか]はともかく、｜最後[さいご]まで｜全力[ぜんりょく]を｜尽[つ]くしたことに｜意味[いみ]がある。

related.note: を問わず means 'regardless of any value of X'; はともかく sets one specific X aside to focus on Y.

title: はもとより
meaning: not to mention ~; let alone ~; of course ~, and also
summary: 〜はもとより presents X as an obvious given ('X, of course') and then adds Y as a further, often more notable case — 'not only X but also Y'. It is formal and written. The Y that follows usually carries も or まで ('even Y').
structure: Noun ＋ はもとより ＋ Noun ＋ も／まで
pitfalls: X はもとより treats X as taken for granted and adds Y; the second item normally carries も/まで.
It is formal and written; in speech はもちろん gives the same 'not to mention' sense more casually.

examples.ja: この温泉は国内はもとより、海外からの観光客にも人気がある。
examples.en: This hot spring is popular not only domestically but with tourists from abroad as well.
examples.f: この｜温泉[おんせん]は｜国内[こくない]はもとより、｜海外[かいがい]からの｜観光[かんこう]｜客[きゃく]にも｜人気[にんき]がある。

examples.ja: 彼は英語はもとより、フランス語やスペイン語まで話せる。
examples.en: He speaks not just English but even French and Spanish.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜英語[えいご]はもとより、フランス｜語[ご]やスペイン｜語[ご]まで｜話[はな]せる。

synonyms.note: はもちろん is the everyday equivalent; はもとより says the same thing in a more formal, written register.

related.note: だけでなく plainly adds 'not only X but Y'; はもとより frames X as an obvious given first.
ばかりか adds a stronger, sometimes surprising Y; はもとより simply treats X as a matter of course.

title: 反面
meaning: on the other hand; while; but at the same time
summary: 〜反面 attaches to a clause to point out a contrasting side of the very same thing — one quality alongside its opposite. 便利な反面 = 'convenient, but on the other side…'. The two facets belong to a single subject.
pitfalls: It contrasts two sides of one and the same subject; use 一方で to contrast two different subjects or situations.
With な-adjectives use な (便利な反面) and with nouns use である (医者である反面).

examples.ja: この仕事は収入が高い反面、責任もとても重い。
examples.en: This job pays well, but on the other side the responsibility is very heavy too.
examples.f: この｜仕事[しごと]は｜収入[しゅうにゅう]が｜高[たか]い｜反面[はんめん]、｜責任[せきにん]もとても｜重[おも]い。

examples.ja: 都会の生活は便利な反面、家賃がとても高い。
examples.en: City life is convenient, but on the flip side the rent is very high.
examples.f: ｜都会[とかい]の｜生活[せいかつ]は｜便利[べんり]な｜反面[はんめん]、｜家賃[やちん]がとても｜高[たか]い。

related.note: 一方で contrasts two separate things; 反面 contrasts two sides of the same one.
代わりに frames a trade-off ('in exchange'); 反面 just notes an opposite quality coexisting.

title: ふうに
meaning: in such a way; like this/that; in the manner of
summary: ふうに (from 風, 'style/manner') describes the manner or style of an action — こんなふうに = 'like this', どんなふうに = 'in what way'. After a clause with という it means 'in a … sort of way'. It points at how something is done or how it comes across.
structure: こんな／そんな／あんな／どんな ＋ ふうに
Sentence ＋ という ＋ ふうに
pitfalls: Here 風 is read ふう and means 'manner/style'; don't confuse it with かぜ ('wind'), which uses the same kanji.
With demonstratives use こんな／そんな／あんな／どんな ＋ ふうに, not こんなに.

examples.ja: どんなふうに説明すれば、分かってもらえるだろう。
examples.en: In what way should I explain it so they'll understand?
examples.f: どんなふうに｜説明[せつめい]すれば、｜分[わ]かってもらえるだろう。

examples.ja: 彼はいつも、自分だけが正しいというふうに話す。
examples.en: He always talks as if only he were in the right.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はいつも、｜自分[じぶん]だけが｜正[ただ]しいというふうに｜話[はな]す。

synonyms.note: みたい compares to an example ('like ~'); ふうに points at the manner or style of doing something.

related.note: とおりに means 'exactly as specified'; ふうに describes a general manner, often vaguer.

title: まい
meaning: surely won't ~; I have no intention of ~ (literary negative)
summary: まい is a literary negative auxiliary with two senses: negative conjecture ('surely won't / probably not', ≈ ないだろう) and negative volition ('I will not / I refuse to', ≈ しないつもりだ). It attaches to the dictionary form; with ichidan verbs and する the stem is also used (見まい／すまい). It sounds formal or old-fashioned.
structure: する → するまい／すまい、来る → 来るまい／来まい
pitfalls: Two meanings: with a third person it is usually 'surely won't' (conjecture); with the speaker it is 'I won't / I refuse' (volition).
It is literary; everyday Japanese uses ないだろう for the guess and ないつもりだ for the intention.

examples.ja: こんな失敗は二度とするまいと、心に決めた。
examples.en: I resolved never to make this kind of mistake again.
examples.f: こんな｜失敗[しっぱい]は｜二度[にど]とするまいと、｜心[こころ]に｜決[き]めた。

examples.ja: 彼女ほどの実力があれば、この試験に落ちることはあるまい。
examples.en: With ability like hers, surely she won't fail this exam.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]ほどの｜実力[じつりょく]があれば、この｜試験[しけん]に｜落[お]ちることはあるまい。

antonyms.note: ようと思う states the intention to do something; まい (volitional sense) states the intention not to.

related.note: だろう is positive conjecture ('probably will'); まい is its negative literary counterpart ('surely won't').
べきではない says one shouldn't (obligation); まい voices the speaker's own resolve not to, or a negative guess.

title: まだしも
meaning: would be acceptable by comparison; if it were only ~, fine, but ~
summary: まだしも marks something as still tolerable compared with a worse alternative — 'X would be one thing, but Y is too much'. It very often appears as ならまだしも: X ならまだしも Y = 'if it were just X, fine, but Y…'. It concedes X grudgingly in order to condemn Y.
structure: まだしも ＋ Noun／Clause ［the less-bad option］
pitfalls: It is comparative: X is not good, only 'less bad' than Y; don't read まだしも as X being genuinely fine.
It very often appears as 〜ならまだしも, setting up the tolerable case before the intolerable one.

examples.ja: 一度だけならまだしも、同じミスを何度も繰り返すのは困る。
examples.en: Once would be one thing, but repeating the same mistake over and over is a problem.
examples.f: ｜一[いち]｜度[ど]だけならまだしも、｜同[おな]じミスを｜何[なん]｜度[ど]も｜繰り返[くりかえ]すのは｜困[こま]る。

examples.ja: 子供ならまだしも、大人がそんなことで泣くのは恥ずかしい。
examples.en: If it were a child, all right, but for an adult to cry over such a thing is embarrassing.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]ならまだしも、｜大人[おとな]がそんなことで｜泣[な]くのは｜恥[は]ずかしい。

synonyms.note: くらいなら rejects an option in favor of a better one; ならまだしも grudgingly accepts the lesser one while condemning a worse one.

related.note: the なら here is the ordinary conditional; まだしも adds the 'that much would be tolerable' judgement.

title: ままに
meaning: as ~; just as ~; at the mercy of; letting it happen
summary: ままに means 'just as (something is or tells you)', going along with a force or desire rather than acting on one's own will — 気の向くままに ('as the mood takes me'), 言われるままに ('just as one is told'). It conveys yielding to whatever drives the action.
pitfalls: This ままに means 'yielding to / just as', driven by an outside force or impulse; it differs from plain まま ('an unchanged state'), though they share the word まま.
It appears in set phrases: 足の向くままに, 思いのままに, 言われるままに.

examples.ja: 彼は感情の赴くままに、思ったことをそのまま口にした。
examples.en: He said whatever came to mind, just as his emotions drove him.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜感情[かんじょう]の｜赴[おもむ]くままに、｜思[おも]ったことをそのまま｜口[くち]にした。

examples.ja: 客は店員に勧められるままに、高い商品を買ってしまった。
examples.en: The customer, simply going along with the clerk's recommendations, ended up buying an expensive item.
examples.f: ｜客[きゃく]は｜店員[てんいん]に｜勧[すす]められるままに、｜高[たか]い｜商品[しょうひん]を｜買[か]ってしまった。

related.note: まま states that a condition stays unchanged; ままに adds the sense of yielding to a force or instruction.
とおりに follows a specified way exactly; ままに passively goes along with whatever drives it.

title: 万が一
meaning: if by any chance; in the unlikely event; just in case
summary: 万が一 (literally 'one in ten thousand') introduces a remote, usually undesirable possibility — 'if by some chance / in the unlikely event'. As an adverb it pairs with a conditional (たら/ば/なら) and often prepares for the worst. It can also work as a noun: 万が一に備える ('prepare for any eventuality').
structure: 万が一 ＋ Verb［たら／ば／なら］
万が一 ＋ に備える／のこと
pitfalls: It flags a low-probability, usually bad case; it is not the neutral 'if' of もし, which covers ordinary conditions.
It is commonly followed by a conditional clause (万が一失敗したら) or used as a noun (万が一に備える).

examples.ja: 万が一事故が起きたら、すぐにこの番号に連絡してください。
examples.en: In the unlikely event of an accident, please call this number right away.
examples.f: ｜万が一[まんがいち]｜事故[じこ]が｜起[お]きたら、すぐにこの｜番号[ばんごう]に｜連絡[れんらく]してください。

examples.ja: 万が一のために、非常食を用意しておいたほうがいい。
examples.en: Just in case, you had better keep some emergency food ready.
examples.f: ｜万が一[まんがいち]のために、｜非[ひ]｜常食[じょうしょく]を｜用意[ようい]しておいたほうがいい。

synonyms.note: もし marks any hypothetical; 万が一 adds that the case is remote and usually unwelcome.

related.note: たとえ〜ても concedes 'even if'; 万が一 sets up a rare possibility to prepare for, not to concede.

title: もう少しで
meaning: almost; nearly; came close to (but didn't)
summary: もう少しで says that something almost happened but was narrowly avoided — 'nearly / came within an inch of'. It usually pairs with ところだった, describing an outcome that did not actually occur. The 'not quite' nuance is the point.
structure: もう少しで ＋ Verb ＋ ところだった
pitfalls: It describes a near miss — the thing did NOT happen; もう少しで転ぶところだった means you did not actually fall.
It is frequently completed by ところだった to mark the averted result.

examples.ja: もう少しで終電に乗り遅れるところだった。
examples.en: I almost missed the last train.
examples.f: もう｜少[すこ]しで｜終電[しゅうでん]に｜乗り遅[のりおく]れるところだった。

examples.ja: もう少しで約束を忘れるところだったが、友達が電話をくれた。
examples.en: I nearly forgot about our plans, but my friend gave me a call.
examples.f: もう｜少[すこ]しで｜約束[やくそく]を｜忘[わす]れるところだったが、｜友達[ともだち]が｜電話[でんわ]をくれた。

synonyms.note: ところだった marks the averted result itself; もう少しで adds 'by a small margin' and usually leads into it.

title: もかまわず
meaning: without caring about ~; heedless of ~; paying no mind to ~
summary: 〜もかまわず (も構わず) means acting without concern for something that would normally give one pause — 人目もかまわず ('heedless of others' eyes'). The doer goes ahead despite X, ignoring what X would ordinarily demand.
structure: Sentence ＋ の ＋ もかまわず
pitfalls: X もかまわず means the doer disregards X, usually something they arguably should mind (人目, 服が汚れるの); it is not a neutral 'regardless'.
構う here is in the negative ず-form, and the phrase is fixed as 〜もかまわず.

examples.ja: 彼女は人目もかまわず、大声で泣き出した。
examples.en: Heedless of the people around her, she burst into loud tears.
examples.f: ｜彼女[かのじょ]は｜人目[ひとめ]もかまわず、｜大声[おおごえ]で｜泣[な]き｜出[だ]した。

examples.ja: 彼は服が汚れるのもかまわず、子供と一緒に地面に座った。
examples.en: Not caring that his clothes would get dirty, he sat down on the ground with the children.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜服[ふく]が｜汚[よご]れるのもかまわず、｜子供[こども]と｜一緒[いっしょ]に｜地面[じめん]に｜座[すわ]った。

related.note: にもかかわらず means 'despite (a fact)'; もかまわず stresses that the doer pays X no mind.
を問わず means 'regardless of which/any'; もかまわず means acting without heeding one specific concern.

title: ものか・もんか
meaning: as if!; there's no way ~; I'll never ~ (emphatic denial)
summary: 〜ものか (casual もんか) is an emphatic rhetorical negation — the speaker forcefully denies or refuses. 負けるものか = 'as if I'd lose! / I'll never lose'. It expresses defiant determination or scorn, roughly 'there's no way that…'. It is a spoken pattern; もんか is the most colloquial.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ ものか／もんか
な-adjective／Noun ＋ な ＋ ものか／もんか
pitfalls: Though it contains no negative word, it means a strong negative: 行くものか = 'I'm absolutely not going', not 'shall I go?'.
It is emotional and casual; もんか is the most colloquial, while ものか in writing sounds emphatic and defiant.

examples.ja: あんな失礼な店に、二度と行くものか。
examples.en: As if I'd ever go to such a rude shop again!
examples.f: あんな｜失礼[しつれい]な｜店[みせ]に、｜二度[にど]と｜行[い]くものか。

examples.ja: こんなところで諦めてなるものか。
examples.en: There's no way I'm giving up here.
examples.f: こんなところで｜諦[あきら]めてなるものか。

synonyms.note: わけがない objectively states 'there's no way'; ものか adds the speaker's defiant emotion and refusal.
はずがない denies on logical grounds; ものか is a heated, personal 'as if!'.

title: ものがある
meaning: there is something ~ about it; really is ~; you can genuinely feel ~
summary: 〜ものがある says that something strongly possesses a certain quality, which the speaker senses — 心を打つものがある ('there is something moving about it'). It voices a heartfelt impression that X genuinely has some quality worth noting, warmer and more evaluative than a plain 〜だ.
structure: な-adjective ＋ な ＋ ものがある
pitfalls: It expresses the speaker's felt impression that X truly has some quality; it is warmer and more evaluative than a plain statement.
The subject is usually an experience, work, or performance that evokes the feeling, not a concrete object one 'has'.

examples.ja: 彼の長年の努力には、心を打つものがある。
examples.en: There is something truly moving about his many years of effort.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]の｜長年[ながねん]の｜努力[どりょく]には、｜心[こころ]を｜打[う]つものがある。

examples.ja: この作品の完成度の高さには、驚くべきものがある。
examples.en: The sheer polish of this work is genuinely astonishing.
examples.f: この｜作品[さくひん]の｜完成[かんせい]｜度[ど]の｜高[たか]さには、｜驚[おどろ]くべきものがある。

related.note: ものだ states a general truth or heartfelt exclamation; ものがある points to a specific quality the speaker strongly senses.

title: ものだから
meaning: because ~; the reason is ~ (explaining or excusing)
summary: 〜ものだから gives a reason, often as an excuse for something unexpected or beyond one's control — 'it's because…'. It stresses that the cause naturally led to the result, so the speaker isn't fully to blame. It is more emotive and self-justifying than a plain から.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ ものだから
な-adjective ＋ な ＋ ものだから
Noun ＋ な ＋ ものだから
pitfalls: It usually explains or excuses an unexpected result, leaning on 'the cause was strong, so naturally…'; a plain から is a neutral 'because'.
With な-adjectives and nouns use な: 不便なものだから, 学生なものだから.

examples.ja: 電車が急に止まったものだから、会議に遅れてしまった。
examples.en: The train stopped all of a sudden, so I ended up late for the meeting.
examples.f: ｜電車[でんしゃ]が｜急[きゅう]に｜止[と]まったものだから、｜会議[かいぎ]に｜遅[おく]れてしまった。

examples.ja: あまりに眠かったものだから、つい返信するのを忘れていた。
examples.en: I was just so sleepy that I carelessly forgot to reply.
examples.f: あまりに｜眠[ねむ]かったものだから、つい｜返信[へんしん]するのを｜忘[わす]れていた。

synonyms.note: もので／ものですから is the same explanatory 'because', a touch softer and more polite; ものだから is more emphatic.
ので is a neutral, polite 'because'; ものだから adds an excusing, 'it couldn't be helped' tone.

related.note: ことから draws an objective conclusion 'from the fact that'; ものだから gives an emotive reason or excuse.

title: ものですから・もので
kana: ものですから・もので
meaning: because ~; you see; my excuse is ~ (polite explanation)
summary: 〜ものですから (casual もので) softly explains a reason, often apologetically — 'it's just that… / you see'. It is the polite, more deferential cousin of ものだから, common when excusing oneself. ものですから is more formal, もので a little lighter.
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ ものですから／もので
な-adjective／Noun ＋ な ＋ ものですから／もので
pitfalls: ものですから is the polite/formal form; もので is a shorter, still-soft version — both give a humble reason, gentler than から.
With nouns and な-adjectives insert な: 初めてなものですから.

examples.ja: まだ慣れないものですから、少しお時間をいただけますか。
examples.en: I'm not used to this yet, you see, so could I have a little time?
examples.f: まだ｜慣[な]れないものですから、｜少[すこ]しお｜時間[じかん]をいただけますか。

examples.ja: 急ぎの用がありましたもので、先に失礼いたしました。
examples.en: I had an urgent matter, so I took my leave ahead of you.
examples.f: ｜急[いそ]ぎの｜用[よう]がありましたもので、｜先[さき]に｜失礼[しつれい]いたしました。

synonyms.note: ものだから is the plainer, more emphatic version; ものですから／もので is politer and more apologetic.
ので is a straightforwardly polite 'because'; ものですから frames the reason as a humble excuse.

title: ものではない
meaning: shouldn't ~; it's not something one does (social norm)
summary: 〜ものではない states that an action goes against common sense or good manners — 'one shouldn't do that / it's not a thing people do'. It appeals to a general social norm rather than a specific rule, and is often used to admonish. Its affirmative 〜ものだ says 'that's how one ought to'.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ ものではない
Verb［dictionary form］＋ もんじゃない（casual）
pitfalls: It scolds based on general decency ('people just don't do that'), not a specific prohibition like てはいけない.
Contrast it with 〜ものだ ('one ought to / that's how it is'); ものではない is its normative negative.

examples.ja: 食べ物を粗末にするものではない。
examples.en: You shouldn't treat food carelessly.
examples.f: ｜食べ物[たべもの]を｜粗末[そまつ]にするものではない。

examples.ja: 人の悪口を、そう簡単に口にするものではない。
examples.en: One shouldn't speak ill of others so lightly.
examples.f: ｜人[ひと]の｜悪口[わるぐち]を、そう｜簡単[かんたん]に｜口[くち]にするものではない。

synonyms.note: べきではない says something is wrong to do by principle; ものではない appeals to common decency and social sense.

related.note: ものだ (affirmative) says 'one ought to / that's how it is'; ものではない is its normative 'one shouldn't'.

title: ものなら
meaning: if (one could) ~; if it were possible to ~ (but it's hard)
summary: 〜ものなら follows a potential verb to set up a difficult or unlikely 'if you could…' — できるものなら ('if it were at all possible'). It implies the thing is hard to achieve, and the main clause says what one would then do, often a wish. Note the separate, harsher 〜（よ）うものなら pattern.
structure: Verb［volitional］＋ ものなら ［if you dare］
pitfalls: With a potential verb it means 'if you could (but it's hard)': 戻れるものなら戻りたい ('I'd go back if only I could').
Don't confuse it with 〜（よ）うものなら (volitional + ものなら), which warns of dire consequences 'if one were to…'.

examples.ja: 帰れるものなら、今すぐ故郷に帰りたい。
examples.en: If only I could, I'd go back to my hometown right now.
examples.f: ｜帰[かえ]れるものなら、｜今[いま]すぐ｜故郷[こきょう]に｜帰[かえ]りたい。

examples.ja: できるものなら、あの日に戻ってやり直したい。
examples.en: If it were at all possible, I'd go back to that day and start over.
examples.f: できるものなら、あの｜日[ひ]に｜戻[もど]ってやり｜直[なお]したい。

synonyms.note: なら is a plain conditional; ものなら adds that the condition is hard or unlikely to meet.

related.note: 〜ようものなら (volitional) warns of dire results 'if one were to'; ものなら (potential) wishes 'if only one could'.

title: ものの
meaning: although ~; even though ~; ~ but
summary: 〜ものの concedes a fact and then presents something that runs counter to what it would lead you to expect — 'although X, (nevertheless) Y'. X is acknowledged as true, yet Y falls short of or contradicts the natural expectation. It is formal and written.
structure: な-adjective ＋ な／である ＋ ものの
Noun ＋ である ＋ ものの
pitfalls: The first clause is admitted as true; the second undercuts the expectation drawn from it — 'bought it, but haven't used it'.
It is written and formal; in speech けれど(も) covers the same 'although' more casually.

examples.ja: 新しいパソコンを買ったものの、忙しくてまだ一度も使っていない。
examples.en: Although I bought a new computer, I've been so busy I haven't used it even once.
examples.f: ｜新[あたら]しいパソコンを｜買[か]ったものの、｜忙[いそが]しくてまだ｜一[いち]｜度[ど]も｜使[つか]っていない。

examples.ja: 頭では理解しているものの、実際にやってみると難しい。
examples.en: Although I understand it in my head, when I actually try it, it's difficult.
examples.f: ｜頭[あたま]では｜理解[りかい]しているものの、｜実際[じっさい]にやってみると｜難[むずか]しい。

synonyms.note: けれども is an everyday 'but/although'; ものの is its more formal, written counterpart.
ながらも also concedes 'even while'; ものの concedes a completed fact, then reverses the expectation.

related.note: くせに concedes with blame or reproach; ものの is neutral concession.

title: もまた
meaning: ... too; ... as well (emphatic, literary)
summary: もまた is an emphatic, somewhat literary version of the particle も 'too / also'. Adding また reinforces that the item belongs to the same category as something already stated — 私もまた = 'I, too (just like the others)'. It attaches to a noun that is the topic and appears mainly in written or formal speech.
pitfalls: It is stronger and more literary than plain も; in casual conversation a simple も is more natural.
The また here is not the sentence adverb また ('again / moreover'); it fuses with も to emphasize 'likewise'.

examples.ja: 私もまた、同じ問題でずっと悩んでいました。
examples.en: I, too, had been troubled by the very same problem all along.
examples.f: ｜私[わたし]もまた、｜同[おな]じ｜問題[もんだい]でずっと｜悩[なや]んでいました。

examples.ja: 自然もまた、人間の暮らしを支える大切な存在である。
examples.en: Nature, too, is a precious presence that sustains human life.
examples.f: ｜自然[しぜん]もまた、｜人間[にんげん]の｜暮[く]らしを｜支[ささ]える｜大切[たいせつ]な｜存在[そんざい]である。

synonyms.note: Plain も simply adds 'too'; もまた lends emphasis and a literary tone.

title: やがて
meaning: before long; in time; eventually
summary: やがて is an adverb meaning 'before long, in time, eventually'. It presents something as coming about through the natural passage of time — the situation moves toward the stated outcome without much delay. It has a narrative, written flavor and describes an approximate near future rather than a fixed time.
pitfalls: It marks a natural, not-too-distant progression of time; it is not 'finally, after much effort', which is ついに.
It names an approximate near future, so it does not pair with an exact clock time or date.

examples.ja: 子供たちの笑い声も、やがて聞こえなくなった。
examples.en: Before long, even the children's laughter had faded away.
examples.f: ｜子供[こども]たちの｜笑い声[わらいごえ]も、やがて｜聞[き]こえなくなった。

examples.ja: 努力を続けていれば、やがて結果はついてくるだろう。
examples.en: If you keep making an effort, results will come in time.
examples.f: ｜努力[どりょく]を｜続[つづ]けていれば、やがて｜結果[けっか]はついてくるだろう。

related.note: ついに marks an endpoint reached at last, often after long effort; やがて is 'before long', stressing a smooth passage of time.
結局 sums up how things turned out in the end; やがて simply says the next stage arrives soon.

title: やら〜やら
meaning: what with ... and ... (and other things)
summary: やら〜やら lists two representative items — nouns, verbs, or adjectives — while implying there are others besides. It often carries a nuance of things being troublesome, chaotic, or overwhelming, so it suits situations of busyness or mixed feelings: 荷物やら書類やら = 'what with luggage and papers and all'.
structure: Noun ＋ やら ＋ Noun ＋ やら
Verb／Adjective［plain form］＋ やら ＋ Verb／Adjective［plain form］＋ やら
pitfalls: It tends to convey that the listed things pile up into something troublesome or confusing, unlike the neutral listing of とか.
The items should be of the same type (two nouns, two adjectives), and the pattern implies 'and others', not an exhaustive list.

examples.ja: 引っ越しの日は、荷造りやら手続きやらで一日じゅうばたばたしていた。
examples.en: On moving day, what with the packing and the paperwork and everything, I was in a rush the whole day.
examples.f: ｜引っ越[ひっこ]しの｜日[ひ]は、｜荷造[にづく]りやら｜手続[てつづ]きやらで｜一[いち]｜日[にち]じゅうばたばたしていた。

examples.ja: 合格の知らせを聞いて、うれしいやら信じられないやら、複雑な気持ちだった。
examples.en: Hearing I had passed, I felt happy and disbelieving and all sorts of things — it was a complicated feeling.
examples.f: ｜合格[ごうかく]の｜知[し]らせを｜聞[き]いて、うれしいやら｜信[しん]じられないやら、｜複雑[ふくざつ]な｜気持[きも]ちだった。

synonyms.note: とか〜とか lists examples neutrally; やら〜やら adds a sense of trouble, disorder, or being overwhelmed.

related.note: 〜たり〜たり lists representative actions neutrally; やら〜やら lists items with an exasperated or busy nuance.

title: ようか〜まいか
meaning: whether or not to do (deliberating)
summary: 〜ようか〜まいか expresses inner deliberation about whether to do something or not: 行こうか行くまいか = 'whether to go or not'. It joins the volitional (I'll do) with まい (I won't / negative volition), so the speaker is weighing two courses and wavering. It has a slightly literary, reflective tone.
structure: Verb［volitional］＋ か ＋ Verb［dictionary form］＋ まいか
pitfalls: The same verb appears twice — once in the volitional, once with まい: 話そうか話すまいか, not a mixed pair.
For する and くる, expect しようか／するまい（すまい）and こようか／くるまい（こまい）rather than an added -oumai form.

examples.ja: 彼に本当のことを話そうか話すまいか、ずっと迷っている。
examples.en: I keep wavering over whether or not to tell him the truth.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]に｜本当[ほんとう]のことを｜話[はな]そうか｜話[はな]すまいか、ずっと｜迷[まよ]っている。

examples.ja: その会に参加しようか参加するまいか、返事を先延ばしにしていた。
examples.en: Unable to decide whether or not to join that gathering, I kept putting off my reply.
examples.f: その｜会[かい]に｜参加[さんか]しようか｜参加[さんか]するまいか、｜返事[へんじ]を｜先[さき]｜延[の]ばしにしていた。

related.note: まい alone states 'won't / probably not'; ようか〜まいか pairs it with the volitional to show two-way deliberation.
ようと思う states a formed intention to act; ようか〜まいか is the earlier stage of still wavering between doing and not.

title: 要するに
meaning: in short; to sum up; essentially
summary: 要するに is an adverbial phrase that introduces a concise restatement of what was just said — 'in short, essentially, to put it briefly'. The speaker boils a longer account down to its core point, often cutting through detail to the conclusion that really matters.
pitfalls: It restates the essence in fewer words; it is not a cause-and-effect 'therefore', so it summarizes rather than draws a logical consequence.
What follows is the speaker's own paraphrase of the gist, so it usually condenses several points into one.

examples.ja: 彼はいろいろと理由を並べたが、要するにお金がないということだ。
examples.en: He lined up all sorts of reasons, but in short, it comes down to having no money.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]はいろいろと｜理由[りゆう]を｜並[なら]べたが、｜要[よう]するにお｜金[かね]がないということだ。

examples.ja: 細かい点はさておき、要するにこの計画には賛成だ。
examples.en: Setting the fine details aside, in short, I am in favor of this plan.
examples.f: ｜細[こま]かい｜点[てん]はさておき、｜要[よう]するにこの｜計画[けいかく]には｜賛成[さんせい]だ。

synonyms.note: つまり restates 'in other words'; 要するに specifically frames the restatement as a boiled-down summary of the essentials.
ということだ concludes 'it amounts to ~'; 要するに opens the sentence to signal a summary is coming.

title: ようでは・ようじゃ
meaning: if (things go / continue) this way ... (bad result)
summary: 〜ようでは presents a situation — often an undesirable habit or state — and says that if it holds, a negative consequence follows: こんな簡単な問題も解けないようでは… = 'if you can't even solve a problem this simple ...'. The second clause is typically a warning or a judgment that things won't work out. ようじゃ is the casual contraction.
structure: Verb［plain form］＋ ようでは／ようじゃ
pitfalls: It leads to a negative evaluation or outcome ('won't succeed / no good'); it is not used to introduce a happy result.
Do not confuse it with ようではないか (a 'let's ~' exhortation); ようでは here is a conditional 'if this way'.

examples.ja: こんな簡単な問題も解けないようでは、試験に合格するのは難しい。
examples.en: If you can't even solve a simple problem like this, passing the exam will be tough.
examples.f: こんな｜簡単[かんたん]な｜問題[もんだい]も｜解[と]けないようでは、｜試験[しけん]に｜合格[ごうかく]するのは｜難[むずか]しい。

examples.ja: 毎晩こんなに遅くまで残業するようじゃ、そのうち体を壊してしまうよ。
examples.en: If you're going to work overtime this late every night, you'll wreck your health before long.
examples.f: ｜毎晩[まいばん]こんなに｜遅[おそ]くまで｜残業[ざんぎょう]するようじゃ、そのうち｜体[からだ]を｜壊[こわ]してしまうよ。

related.note: Looks similar but opposite in use: ようではないか urges 'let's do ~', while ようでは warns 'if it's like this ~'.
〜限り says 'as long as X holds, ~'; ようでは narrows this to an undesirable state leading to a bad result.

title: ようではないか
meaning: let's ...; why don't we ... (formal exhortation)
summary: 〜ようではないか is a formal, rhetorical exhortation built on the volitional — 'let us ~, shall we not ~'. The speaker calls on the listeners to join in an action, so it is common in speeches, editorials, and appeals. ようじゃないか is the more colloquial variant of the same call to action.
structure: Verb［volitional］＋ ではないか／じゃないか
pitfalls: It attaches to the volitional (乗り越えよう＋ではないか); this is exhortation, distinct from the conditional 〜ようでは ('if this way ~').
The tone is oratorical and formal; in ordinary conversation a plain volitional or 〜ましょう is more natural.

examples.ja: 困難な時こそ、みんなで力を合わせて乗り越えようではないか。
examples.en: It is precisely in hard times that we should join forces and pull through — shall we not?
examples.f: ｜困難[こんなん]な｜時[とき]こそ、みんなで｜力[ちから]を｜合[あ]わせて｜乗り越[のりこ]えようではないか。

examples.ja: この美しい町の自然を、私たちの手で守ろうではないか。
examples.en: Let us protect the nature of this beautiful town with our own hands.
examples.f: この｜美[うつく]しい｜町[まち]の｜自然[しぜん]を、｜私[わたし]たちの｜手[て]で｜守[まも]ろうではないか。

related.note: じゃないか seeks the listener's agreement ('isn't it?'); ようではないか builds on the volitional to urge joint action.
ようと思う is one's private intention to act; ようではないか openly rallies others to act together.

title: よほど・よっぽど
meaning: considerably; to a great extent; far more
summary: よほど is an adverb meaning 'to a considerable degree, much (more)'. It often draws an inference that a situation must be extreme from the evidence at hand (よほど疲れていたのだろう = 'must have been really tired'), and it also strengthens comparisons (よほどいい = 'far better'). よっぽど is the more colloquial, emphatic form.
pitfalls: In the inference use it commonly pairs with のだろう／らしい: よほど〜のだろう = 'must have been quite ~'.
よっぽど is casual; it also colors a suppressed impulse — よっぽど言おうかと思った = 'I very nearly said it'.

examples.ja: 彼は挨拶もせずに帰ってしまった。よほど機嫌が悪かったのだろう。
examples.en: He left without even saying goodbye. He must have been in a really bad mood.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜挨拶[あいさつ]もせずに｜帰[かえ]ってしまった。よほど｜機嫌[きげん]が｜悪[わる]かったのだろう。

examples.ja: この店のほうが、駅前の店よりよっぽど安い。
examples.en: This shop is far cheaper than the one in front of the station.
examples.f: この｜店[みせ]のほうが、｜駅前[えきまえ]の｜店[みせ]よりよっぽど｜安[やす]い。

synonyms.note: さぞ guesses sympathetically at how someone must feel; よほど also infers a strong degree but is not limited to feelings and can intensify comparisons.

related.note: ほど marks a degree or extent as a benchmark; よほど is a fixed adverb meaning 'to a considerable degree'.

title: よりしかたがない
meaning: have no choice but to; nothing to do but
summary: 〜よりしかたがない (also よりしかたない) attaches to a dictionary-form verb to say there is no option other than doing it — 'there's nothing to do but ~'. It resigns the speaker to the only remaining course of action, usually reluctantly, when circumstances leave no alternative.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ よりしかたがない
pitfalls: The verb before より stays in dictionary form: 歩いて帰るよりしかたがない, not 帰ったより.
It carries a tone of reluctant resignation; it is nearly identical in meaning to よりほかない and ざるを得ない.

examples.ja: 終電を逃してしまったので、歩いて帰るよりしかたがなかった。
examples.en: I missed the last train, so I had no choice but to walk home.
examples.f: ｜終電[しゅうでん]を｜逃[のが]してしまったので、｜歩[ある]いて｜帰[かえ]るよりしかたがなかった。

examples.ja: 上司の指示である以上、その方針に従うよりしかたがない。
examples.en: Since it is the boss's instruction, there is nothing to do but follow that policy.
examples.f: ｜上司[じょうし]の｜指示[しじ]である｜以上[いじょう]、その｜方針[ほうしん]に｜従[したが]うよりしかたがない。

synonyms.note: よりほかない is a near-identical twin; both mean 'no choice but to', with よりほかない sounding a touch more formal.
ざるを得ない ('cannot help but') is a more formal, written equivalent attaching to the ない-stem.

related.note: 〜しかない also says 'the only option is ~'; よりしかたがない specifically frames it as resigned helplessness.

title: よりほかない
meaning: have no choice but to; no option besides
summary: 〜よりほかない (also よりほかはない) attaches to a dictionary-form verb to say there is nothing besides doing it — 'no choice but to ~'. It marks the sole remaining option with a tone of resignation, when no better alternative is available.
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ よりほかない／よりほかはない
pitfalls: Keep the preceding verb in dictionary form: あきらめるよりほかない.
It is a near-synonym of よりしかたがない and ざるを得ない; all express a reluctant, unavoidable choice.

examples.ja: 誰も助けてくれないなら、自分で何とかするよりほかない。
examples.en: If no one will help, I have no choice but to manage it myself somehow.
examples.f: ｜誰[だれ]も｜助[たす]けてくれないなら、｜自分[じぶん]で｜何[なん]とかするよりほかない。

examples.ja: 在庫がないと言われた以上、注文をあきらめるよりほかなかった。
examples.en: Since I was told there was no stock, I had no choice but to give up on the order.
examples.f: ｜在庫[ざいこ]がないと｜言[い]われた｜以上[いじょう]、｜注文[ちゅうもん]をあきらめるよりほかなかった。

synonyms.note: よりしかたがない means the same 'no choice but to'; the two are interchangeable in most contexts.
ざるを得ない is a more formal, written way to say one cannot help but do the action.

related.note: 〜しかない likewise limits things to one option; よりほかない adds a resigned, no-alternative nuance.

title: ろくに〜ない
meaning: not properly; hardly (do something well)
summary: ろくに precedes a negative verb to say something is not done properly, sufficiently, or to a decent standard — 'hardly, not even decently'. It criticizes an inadequate degree or quality of the action, often as a complaint: ろくに寝ていない = 'haven't slept properly'.
pitfalls: It requires a following negative — ろくに〜ない — and cannot stand with an affirmative verb.
It stresses 'not to a proper standard', carrying a critical or complaining tone rather than a plain 'not much'.

examples.ja: このところ忙しくて、ろくに寝ていない。
examples.en: I've been so busy lately that I've hardly slept properly.
examples.f: このところ｜忙[いそが]しくて、ろくに｜寝[ね]ていない。

examples.ja: 彼は説明もろくに聞かずに、作業を始めてしまった。
examples.en: He started the work without even properly listening to the explanation.
examples.f: ｜彼[かれ]は｜説明[せつめい]もろくに｜聞[き]かずに、｜作業[さぎょう]を｜始[はじ]めてしまった。

title: わずかに
meaning: slightly; barely; merely; only a little
summary: わずかに means 'slightly, only a little, barely'. As an adverb it describes a very small degree or change (わずかに動く = move a fraction), and before a quantity it means 'merely, only just' (わずか二年 = a mere two years). Throughout, it emphasizes how small or scarce the amount is.
pitfalls: When modifying a quantity it usually drops に: わずか二年, not わずかに二年.
It highlights smallness or scarcity of degree/amount; it is not the 'only' of identity or scope (that role belongs to だけ／のみ).

examples.ja: 処置のおかげで、痛みがわずかに和らいだ。
examples.en: Thanks to the treatment, the pain eased slightly.
examples.f: ｜処置[しょち]のおかげで、｜痛[いた]みがわずかに｜和[やわ]らいだ。

examples.ja: 開店からわずか二年で、その店は全国に広がった。
examples.en: In a mere two years since opening, that shop spread across the whole country.
examples.f: ｜開店[かいてん]からわずか｜二[に]｜年[ねん]で、その｜店[みせ]は｜全国[ぜんこく]に｜広[ひろ]がった。

related.note: だけ limits to 'only ~ and nothing else'; わずか(に) stresses that the quantity or degree itself is tiny.

title: をきっかけに・がきっかけで
kana: をきっかけに・がきっかけで
romaji: o kikkake ni / ga kikkake de
meaning: with ... as the trigger; taking ... as the start
